This is a comprehensive summary of the birdMonitor: what the project is, what has been done and tested so far, how the code works, how to run it on the cluster, and what to do next, in order of importance.

# 1. Overview and progress

**What birdMonitor is.** An R and SpaDES pipeline that turns bird records and environmental layers into yearly occurrence maps, national and regional indices and confidence intervals for breeding bird species in Germany, 2005 to 2025 (11 species until 21 October; the roster for the first version of the Monitor has 14 since 28 October, see below). It follows the multi-scale meta-model method of Wiedenroth et al. (climate 50 km, landscape 1 km, habitat 200 m, combined by a ridge meta-model) and adds three things: honest out-of-fold weights, a spatial-block bootstrap uncertainty framework that carries uncertainty into every product, and an ensemble of five algorithms (the "big 5").

**The ten things a newcomer must know first** (items 8 to 10 were added on 29 October).

1. The 2005-2021 maps are a hindcast: the habitat model learns from 2022-2025 data only.
2. The intervals show sensitivity to the training data, not uncertainty of counts in the field.
3. All national and regional numbers must be Germany-only; the prediction window is the bounding box of Germany, 35% of which is abroad.
4. The size of the trends depends on how strongly the meta-model is regularised (random-fold or block-fold penalty); the choice is documented in `DECISIONS.md`, 10 October.
5. The baseline climate models are refitted whenever the europe array runs, and the number of trees can change; replicate 0 must be refreshed after a refit (the parity check catches this).
6. On the cluster always run submit scripts with `bash --login`, start every command block with `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor`, and never submit a workflow twice (the scripts refuse unless `FORCE=1`).
7. Never project the German outline with terra or sf in a standalone cluster job: the axis order of EPSG:3035 can come out swapped; use the closed-form `uncOutlineLAEA()`.
8. The preparation changes `inputs/predictors/processed` and `inputs/response/processed` in place (crop to the study area, hedges, new classes). Keep a copy of them first; the clean-run script refuses to start without one in `/data/birds`. Do not test a destructive step locally unless you have checked where `inputs/` really points (see the incident of 21 October).
9. The suffix `_germany` in folder names means "the reporting area" (Germany today), not a rename waiting to happen. The working area is the reporting area plus a buffer, so the final maps still have to be cut to it. Revisit the suffix when a second area is run, and give that run a new name.
10. The probabilities for 2025 are a forecast for the landscape scale: the DDA territory data end in 2024. Habitat and meta-model are trained on 2022 to 2025. Validating the 2025 values is on the list (section 6, P2.15).


# 2. Chronology

What was done, tested, found and changed, day by day from 23 September to 12 October 2026, then the incidents and the decisions as tables. Reconstructed from `DECISIONS.md`, the project memory notes and the git history of the root repo and the four modules. Commit hashes (7 characters) are given so each item can be checked. "Project lead" = Tatiane Micheletti; "assistant" = the Claude sessions that did most of the implementation. Where a source does not say who decided something, the text says "not recorded".

**Caveats.** (1) Dates around midnight 9/10 October are uncertain: the ridge-rule commits are stamped 9 October 23:28, the DECISIONS entry is headed 10 October. (2) Most "tested" statements are quoted from DECISIONS and the memory notes; this document did not re-run anything. (3) Before 25 September only git and one Confluence-derived DECISIONS entry (no day) are available.

## 1. Day by day

### 23 and 24 September (context before the main record)

- **Built (git):** `runClusterTask.R` moved to `tools/` so SpaDES never auto-sources it (`c1d6206`); extended to the meta-model stage (`f7721ee`); routed through real SpaDES (`c96047e`); `--species` filter (`0210c57`); post-hoc Germany crop tool (`07c602a`); the `eve-cluster` skill documenting the UFZ onboarding constraints (`6639c3f`); Anthus pratensis added to the roster (`2108c38`); `sharedRegionalCellSizesM` as the single source of truth for grid sizes (`316d40c`).
- **Decided (team, Confluence):** drop `hedges` as a default covariate (Katrin Boehning-Gaese consulted); drop Milvus milvus from scope (DDA meeting 24 September). EVE account active from 24 September; no real cluster run yet.

### 25 September

- **Built** (branch `feature/reconcile-with-v2-flexible-config`): reconciliation with Lisa Hildebrand's v2 code in seven items: spatial-block-size floor (default 2 x resolution; inputs\_Monitor `bc6cfe7`); configurable thinning distance and breeding-code filter (dataPrep `0567722`, `ace81a8`); Buteo buteo and Sturnus vulgaris landscape data routed through MhB point counts (`10a2154`); BRT starting learning rate per species (models `38a302e`, `9319846`); independent per-scale land use/cover cache check (`e2117db`); hedges toggle (`07b66aa`, `5c09d70`); predictor selection (redesigned three times in the session). Two config CSVs, `runMe.R` wiring, `DECISIONS.md` created (root `8d74eab`).
- **Tested:** synthetic data and mocked functions. Empirical check of the floor bug: Milvus at 30 km landscape, 69.4% of occupied cells had points split across more than one fold before the fix.
- **Found (DDA results meeting, deck of 25 September):** climate contributes 0-1.1% to the meta-model, landscape 8-46%, habitat 46-91%. Weak fits: Lanius collurio, Sturnus vulgaris, Milvus milvus.
- **Why:** Buteo and Sturnus landscape data from MhB counts because the Star data predicted uniformly high (hypothesis: DDA territory counts saturate for very common species). The block floor defaulted to 0, a real bug.

### 26 September

- **Incident:** Anthus pratensis showed "Too few presences (0)" at habitat scale although the raw MhB file has 2295 records. **Cause:** `speciesLookup()` was never updated when the species joined the roster; the filter by German name silently matched zero rows. **Fix:** one canonical species table `speciesCanonical.csv`; the habitat scale filters on the scientific name (root `311b4c2`). After the fix: 576/551/577/591 presences for 2022-2025. The project lead's diagnosis: "We need ONE canonical source!".
- **Found:** at climate scale Anthus pratensis also had 0 presences, for a different reason: the EBBA2 extract (17 July 2026) has no row for it, a real data gap. A minimum-10-presences guard was added.
- **Changed:** an unfittable BRT is a per-species skip, not a crash (models `99176c9` fixes an infinite loop in `optimizeBRT()`); solar radiation dropped for all species; x/y coordinates added as predictors for every species (a spatial trend-surface term, not a random effect); breeding-code filter moved from habitat to landscape scale for Buteo.
- **Tested:** real `gbm.step()` calls on synthetic data; a mocked always-failing `gbm.step()`; a zero-variance species skipped cleanly.

### 27 and 28 September

- **27 Sep:** canonical species table, spatial-term code, detailed `readme.Rmd`.
- **28 Sep, built:** real per-species cache invalidation through `reproducible::Cache()` at 9 points in 3 modules plus a persistent `cache/` folder (the old checks were pure file-existence memoization); CSV-driven config simplification (`resolution_m` consumed per species; `brt_start_lr`, `predictor_mode` and per-scale overrides removed; `dropCollinearPredictors` toggle); fitting years decoupled from prediction years; config CSVs moved to `data/`; silent config bugs fixed (comma-formatted numbers, a misplaced Buteo filter).
- **Tested:** real (non-mocked) fits and `Cache()` calls at every conversion point (a config change for one species recomputes only that species); a two-species run with a 15x coarser override; synthetic rasters at two resolutions per scale.
- **Found:** `evalSDM()` and `blockCVPredictBRT()` were not deterministic run to run (fixed on 5 October). Documented assumption: each scale's fitting window is set by its own survey (climate: EBBA2 2017; landscape: DDA 2005-2025; habitat: MhB 2022-2025), so hindcast risk differs by scale.
- **Principle (project lead):** config CSVs hold ecological decisions; algorithm settings are module constants.

### 29 and 30 September

- **29 Sep, built:** `runIndex_Monitor` as its own module chained into `runMe.R`; `scalesToRun`; new covariates `dist_to_woodland` and `landscape_heterogeneity`; the meta-model under `Cache()`.
- **Found and fixed:** chaining the index step into a live session exposed two latent terra bugs: `c()` of derived rasters zeroes source layers (fixed with `combineLayersSafely()`); a bare `mean()` on a SpatRaster silently falls through to `mean.default()` and returns NA (fixed with namespaced `terra::mean()`; root cause not found).
- **30 Sep, incident:** the pooling step crashed with an `rbind()` column mismatch. Two causes: `Cache()` turned a genuine NULL into the string "NULL", saved as a bogus occurrence file; and the pooling globbed all files of a species with no year filter, mixing 17 stale files with 4 new ones. **Fix:** `isCachedNull()`, a `years` argument and `bind_rows()` (dataPrep `ed7a0f3`, inputs `e67dc80`); the corrupted files were removed by hand. Also fixed: locale-dependent encoding of German names in the raw MhB file. Not resolved: why the live session hit an early `return(NULL)` that a standalone reproduction never did.

### 1 and 2 October

- **1 Oct:** per-species fitting years (`years_override`); the MhB window 2022:2025 applied to every species; Buteo landscape 5 km and thinning corrected; umlauts folded to ASCII; a full-roster timing run prepared (run name `test4`).
- **2 Oct, built:** the whole workflow runnable on EVE for 11 species (root `56417c9`): prep, model arrays, index chain; auto-cancel of dependents if prep fails; stage switch `BIRDMONITOR_STAGE`; personal R library when the system one is read-only; prep without Python, token or internet. The EVE module recipe took several iterations (R 4.6.1 cannot combine with GDAL; final: R 4.5.1 + GDAL 3.10.3 + CMake + ImageMagick + UDUNITS). EVE rejects `--mem`: `--mem-per-cpu` everywhere.
- **Decided (DECISIONS 2 Oct):** pure-ASCII canonical species table plus umlaut folding on both sides of every German-name comparison (Buteo's "Maeusebussard" failed on a Latin-1 vs UTF-8 mismatch); MhB data only from 2022:2025; landscape scales Buteo 5 km and Lanius 700 m (from Lisa's tests: 30 km was worse for Buteo, AUC 0.541 vs 0.622 at 1 km); `reproducible.useMemoise = FALSE` (with it on, the run died with `std::bad_alloc`); 11 species, Milvus stays out.

### 3 and 4 October

- **3 Oct, EVE first setup:** `EVE_GUIDE.md` and one-command `cluster/setup_eve.sh`; smoke test "SMOKETEST: ALL OK"; `TMPDIR` moved to `/work` because EVE's `$TMPDIR` is a RAM disk. **Incident (regrid):** `project()` failed with "area of interest not accepted" (EVE GDAL 3.10 / PROJ 9.4); fixed with `resample()` for same-CRS rasters. **Incident (transfer):** WinSCP "Preserve timestamp" kept old dates and `/work`'s hourly cleaner deletes files whose access time is more than 60 days old, so uploaded land-use and response files vanished silently. Fix: untick the option, `touch` after upload, verify by file counts, byte totals and md5. This cost hours. `/data/birds` requested from WKDV.
- **4 Oct:** while setting up passwordless EVE login, `ssh-keygen` overwrote an existing key and the wiki's `mv config.txt config` replaced `~/.ssh/config`; SSH to GitHub from the PC stopped working. Logged as the assistant's mistake; no effect on results.

### 5 October (busiest day: 36 root commits)

- **First real EVE prep run lost every row.** "Removed N rows with NA covariates" with N = all rows: 100% NA for all 22 layers at the bird points. Diagnosis tools run on EVE (`inspectOccurrence.R`, `diagnoseCovariates.R`, resample and covariate-stack probes, a gbm CPU benchmark). **Finding:** point coordinates were x 2.7-3.5 million / y 4.0-4.7 million: x and y swapped (Germany in EPSG:3035 is x about 4.0-4.7e6, y about 2.7-3.5e6). **Root cause (isolated 15:05-16:34):** if terra does GDAL work first, a later `sf::st_transform(., 3035)` returns x/y swapped; if sf transforms first, it is correct (GDAL 3.10.3 / PROJ 9.4.1 / sf 1.1.3 / terra 1.9-50 on EVE; not reproducible on the PC). **Fix:** `transformToLAEA()` with explicit PROJ string, validated against a closed-form formula; `laeaCoordinates()` stops loudly if x/y look swapped; sf forced to transform first; occurrence cache schema 3. A public reprex for the sf/terra maintainers was written, not sent.
- **Reproducibility groundwork:** fold BRT refits kept and saved; deterministic seeds (`stableSeed`) for CV block assignment, BRT fits, fold refits and ridge CV (closes the 28 September item).
- **Uncertainty option B built** (first as a stand-alone folder so the baseline arrays already queued would not be disturbed, then as SpaDES events in the modules). **Decisions by the project lead:** 90% interval (5th to 95th percentile), all years, CI width plus share of replicates decreasing/increasing as confidence layers, B = 50 first with the ability to add replicates, seeds logged.
- **Evening:** the baseline habitat array ran out of memory on EVE at 13 GB (all years' covariate stacks loaded at once); fixed by loading one year at a time. `optimizeBRT()` now reports the real `gbm.step` error, which `try()` had swallowed.

### 6 October

- **Memory fixes on EVE:** habitat covariates read from a cached file and predicted block by block; habitat years predicted in separate R processes ("chunks"); meta-model reference grid cropped to Germany (738 M to 15 M cells); the index job killed at 32 GB because change rasters were kept in memory, then measured at 20.1 GB peak.
- **Meta-model made honest.** Performance table across species and scales with the meta-model flagged optimistic; non-negative ridge weights via `fitRidgeCv()` (`lower.limits = 0`; previously a scale could get a negative weight and the in-sample AUC of about 0.99 was flattered). **Project lead's decision, same evening: "I NEED the most honest measures of uncertainty as possible."** The ridge weights are now trained on out-of-fold inputs (stacked generalisation), which goes beyond the published method (final weights in-sample). New replicate step `oof` (about 4x the previous per-replicate BRT cost); `ridge` refuses to run without it; out-of-fold failures are fatal, no silent in-sample fallback.
- **Local verification of option B** (Alauda arvensis, 4 replicates, years 2020-2025): replicate 0 reproduces the baseline meta map (maximum difference 0.00002 = the 16-bit storage resolution, correlation 1.000000, ridge coefficients equal to 6 digits); end-to-end rehearsal through the real entry point: identical valid cells, country mean 0.656788 vs 0.656788.
- **Known choice to review (not changed):** the climate-scale resampling block comes out at the 1500 km cap (autocorrelation range 4400 km), about 13 blocks for Europe; sensitivity switch `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_BLOCKMULT`.
- **EVE:** the first uncertainty chain (unconstrained in-sample ridge) was cancelled after the redesign. **Ensemble started** (branch `feature/ensemble`): GLM/GAM/RF fit, predict, refit, block-CV, mean.

### 7 October

- **Honest uncertainty chain finished on EVE** (BRT-only, tag `honest`): 50 replicates, parity OK for all 11 species. Honest meta AUCs 0.71 (Buteo) to 0.95 (Alauda, E. calandra); per-scale AUCs are not comparable across scales. **These preliminary numbers were later invalidated** (see the climate fault below).
- **Method provenance:** Kamp et al. 2021 read in full: DDA species indices are TRIM (Poisson on counts, not applicable to occurrence probabilities); multi-species indicators follow Soldaat et al. 2017 (Monte Carlo, 1000 draws). Our MSI matches that combination step; our "Analytical" index is the older PECBMS method (Gregory 2005 delta) and must not be labelled DDA. A multi-species index after Koerner-Nievergelt 2022 was not implemented (needs absolute abundance).
- **Climate data fault found while explaining last-year drops.** The 2025 climate predictors were impossible (bio1 28.7, bio10 87.7 degrees). Causes in `getMonthlyFile()`: from 2022, tasmin/tasmax came from daily files aggregated as MIN of daily minima / MAX of daily maxima while the monthly product and bioclim use the MEAN (a break at 2022 of about 4-5 K); fill values kept as data (tasmin April 2022 zeros; tasmax April/May 2025 6553.4); 2025 has only January to September. **Consequence:** climate predictions for 2022-2025, exactly the years the meta-model weights are trained on, were unreliable; probably the cause of climate weight 0 for 7 of 11 species. **Root cause of the fill values:** flaky remote reads (`/vsicurl/` partial read failures returned zeros instead of an error). **Fix:** mean; fill values to NA; months with fewer than 90% of days not used; retry and re-read; new `_dmean` cache. The old numbers (Anthus 2025 index 70.8 and so on) must never be shown. A wrong hypothesis was refuted on the way: the Anthus pratensis 2025 drop is not climate (its climate weight is 0).
- **Climate windows rebuilt** on the PC (about 3 h, old windows moved aside, nothing deleted). **Ensemble built:** registry of glm, gam, rf, nn; BRT as a member via fold models; any member set gets its own tag; ensemble bootstrap added (the ensemble refitted inside each replicate, about 4x the cost). Local test (Alauda): landscape block-CV AUC BRT 0.865, GLM 0.878, GAM 0.875, RF 0.871, NN 0.879, ensemble of all five 0.885; habitat BRT 0.936, ensemble 0.946.
- **Storage:** WKDV confirmed `/data/birds`. **Project lead decided not to copy anything until results are final.** Tasks set: regional index uncertainty (10/20/50 km) with cold and hot spots.

### 8 October

- **02:45 everything merged to main.** Local tests with the rebuilt windows: BRT meta (Alauda climate weight 0.63 became 12.3: the bug had suppressed climate weights), ensemble meta (non-negative, honest, AUC 0.957), both uncertainty workflows end to end with parity OK.
- **Morning (EVE):** the four rebuilt window files uploaded; `cluster/rerun_after_climate_fix.sh` moves aside everything built with the buggy climate (never deletes); the BRT-only chain `honest2` queued. **Incident (duplicate jobs):** duplicate meta arrays and index jobs; one cancelled; that evening the submit scripts were made to refuse to run twice (`FORCE=1` overrides).
- **Bray-Curtis turnover** (asked for by the project lead: richness and mean change cannot tell a species swap from no change): added as a fifth community layer and inside each replicate. Unit tests (a swap of 4 of 5 species gives 0.8; no change gives 0).
- **Regional index (10/20/50 km) with uncertainty** built (steps `regionband`, `regionassemble`, `regionindex`). Design by the project lead: German outline applied to the 200 m pixels BEFORE averaging; no smoothing inside replicates, only on the final result; both `shareDecrease` and `shareIncrease`.
- **Finding: the national indices averaged non-German pixels.** The prediction window is the bounding box of Germany: 13.9 M pixels of 200 m, 8.97 M inside Germany. Seven species (Alauda, Anthus, Buteo, E. calandra, Perdix, Saxicola, Vanellus) have predictions over the whole window (35.4% outside Germany); four (E. citrinella, Lanius, Lullula, Sturnus) only inside Germany (their models use `hedges` or `landscape_heterogeneity`). National area means differ up to 55% (Saxicola 0.147 vs 0.095 inside Germany). The first EVE check failed because `terra::project` of the outline returned x/y swapped in a plain terra job; fixed with a closed-form outline (`uncOutlineLAEA()`). **Project lead's decision:** nothing may be computed or predicted outside Germany; always crop all inputs with the study-area outline, not the bounding box. The proper source-level fix comes after the Steering Consortium meeting (the assistant must remind her). For the meeting: mask to Germany and recalculate (the `_germany` copies).
- **Ensemble decisions (project lead):** one variant only, "the big 5" brt, glm, gam, rf, nn. NN pilot: 3 hidden units, decay 0.1, maxit 1000 for all scales.
- **Documents and dates:** Steering Consortium decisions document created. Dates fixed by the project lead: meeting Friday 16 October; all materials due Wednesday 14 October; results and documents for her by Tuesday 13 October midday. Word export only at the end.
- **22:22-22:40 night submission** of the big 5 (baseline plus uncertainty with 25 replicates) and the BRT regional chain. The pre-flight found `nnet` missing on EVE (installed through `setup_uncertainty.sh`). A climate GAM (Alauda) then did not converge and all dependents were cancelled; fix: robust GAM settings; `resume_big5_2026-10-08.sh` depends only on jobs Slurm still knows (finished jobs are forgotten after minutes).

### 9 October

- **Floor/cap result:** no baseline cell mean below 1e-3 except 7 Lullula cells at 10 km; no species-cell ratio above 10 at any grid; max regional index 122; no cell above 200 or below 50. The feared explosion with `minBaseline = 1e-6` does not occur. Recommendation: keep 1e-6 and add DDA-style ratio truncation (above 10) as an inactive documented safeguard. The project lead still wants to discuss it with the DDA.
- **BRT-only parity problem found and explained.** 9 of 11 species OK and the regional grids OK; mismatch for Anthus pratensis (relative area-mean difference 3.4e-3) and Sturnus vulgaris (1.7e-4). A race between the duplicate meta arrays was refuted. Three read-only diagnostic jobs showed that weights, penalty and out-of-fold inputs were identical for all species and that the divergence was in the climate model: the europe array had refitted the climate BRTs on 8 October while replicate 0 held the copy of 6 October, and `gbm.step`'s internal CV is random, so three species got a different tree count (Anthus 1750 vs 2400, Vanellus 2400 vs 2300, Sturnus 1300 vs 1350). Effect at most 0.3% of the national mean. **Fix:** refresh of the three species (`refresh_climate_3species_2026-10-09.sh`); afterwards all 11 species and the three regional grids passed parity. Lesson: after refitting baseline models, re-copy or rerun replicate 0.
- **Big 5 prepare incident:** tasks 3, 7, 11 completed (4-5.4 h, peak 51 GB); tasks 1, 6, 8, 9, 10 failed after 8-22 min with "\<scale> / gam: N replicate fit(s) failed" (one GAM refit error on a bootstrap resample killed the whole batch of its core); tasks 2, 4, 5 ran out of memory above 64 GB. **Fix:** robust GAM refit ladder, per-replicate `tryCatch` (the main fit stands in; logged in `refit_fallbacks.csv`); rerun with 128 GB. Resumed 18:07 (prepare 63257254, band 63257289 with 528 tasks and 24 h each).
- **BRT-only timings:** prepare 0.4 h wall; band 176 tasks, mean 2.87 h, max 10.96 h, wall 13.9 h; summarize 0.5 h; assemble 0.2 h; community 0.3 h.
- **Big 5 baseline finished** (fits, ensemble means, honest meta, index, Germany-only index).

### 10 October (DECISIONS entry; git stamps 9 October 23:00-23:28)

- **Finding:** in the BRT-only run (Germany only, 2025) the baseline combined index (95.6) fell OUTSIDE the 90% interval of its own 50 replicates (mean 97.5, interval 96.1-99.0). Perdix perdix: baseline 91.1, replicates 99.0-100; Vanellus: 90.8 vs 91.3-96.3.
- **Diagnosis** (`tools/diagnoseReplicateBias.R`): the replicate ridge penalties were 2-3 times the baseline's (Buteo 0.17 vs 0.075; E. calandra 0.16 vs 0.042) and the weights shrunk; for Perdix the penalty was 38.7 and all replicate weights were exactly 0 (constant probability, index exactly 100). **Cause:** the replicates chose the penalty (`lambda.1se`) with spatial block folds, the baseline with ten random folds. A bootstrap must repeat the SAME procedure on resampled data.
- **Change:** every replicate uses the baseline's rule (ten random folds; models\_Monitor `e0f5fa8`, root `ebf7f8d`); `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_RIDGEFOLDS=block` restores the old rule. **Caveat to state:** random folds can under-regularise (autocorrelation and duplicated blocks leak between folds); the penalty, and with it the size of the trends, depends on this choice. The earlier block-fold results are kept as the sensitivity analysis (`_old_ridge_blockfolds_2026-10-10/`; the block-fold replicates gave a 2025 combined index of 97.5 against the baseline's 95.6).
- **Redo planned:** BRT-only band stage again (about 14 h wall); big 5 ridge step before its band stage. The first big 5 chain meanwhile ran into the problem below.
- **Big 5 chain fails (10 October 18:13):** prepare task 6 (Emberiza calandra) hit the 24 h limit in the out-of-fold step; its `fit` and `coarse` steps were done (about 19 h), the out-of-fold step had run about 5 h. The other 7 reruns completed. The held band job and everything behind it were cancelled by the dependency rule. The ridge redo for the big 5 was never run.

# 3. How the modules work

Read from the code (file and function names are given so you can check). Where a statement comes from `DECISIONS.md` or `UNCERTAINTY.md` instead of the code it says so. "Unclear" means it could not be settled from the code. This page describes what the code writes; what currently exists on EVE is shown by the monitor scripts (tab 5).

## 0. Conventions used everywhere

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Species roster | `data/speciesCanonical.csv`, `include` column marked "X" gives `sharedSpecies` (`tools/sharedConfig.R`): 14 species since 28 October (11 until 21 October; Milvus milvus, Perdix perdix and Streptopelia turtur are out). `BIRDMONITOR_SPECIES="A b;C d"` restricts a run for debugging. |
| Three scales | **Climate** (Europe, 50 km, EBBA2 atlas data), **landscape** (Germany, 1 km, DDA territories or MhB point counts), **habitat** (Germany, 200 m, MhB point counts). Per-species resolution overrides come from `data/speciesConfig_general.csv` (`resolution_m`; Lanius collurio 700 m and Buteo buteo 5 km landscape). |
| Scale label | `scaleLabel(resolutionM)` gives `scale_50`, `scale_1`, `scale_02` (200 m) and so on: the folder name in `inputs/` and `outputs/`. |
| Meta-model folder label | `metamodelLabel(c(europe=50000, habitat=200, landscape=1000))` gives `metamodel_02_1_50`, always keyed to the SHARED resolutions. |
| Years | `predictionYears = 2005:2025`. Fitting years of landscape and habitat are per species. Habitat years are also the meta-model training years: years before them are hindcasts. `baselineYear = 2005`, `currentYear = 2025`. |
| File names | Latin name with underscores (`Alauda_arvensis`). |
| Run folder | `outputs/<runName>/`; `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` pins it (default `test4`; the clean-run script uses `v2`). |
| Study area | `sharedStudyArea` in `tools/sharedConfig.R` (a country, a region or a shapefile); `BIRDMONITOR_STUDY_AREA="DEU:Sachsen"` overrides it for a test. Buffers: `sharedRecordsBufferM` 1000 m (records, habitat and landscape layers) and 50 km for the climate predictions. `BIRDMONITOR_YEARS=2022:2025` restricts the years for fast local tests (the clean-run script refuses it). |
| Run "tags" | Suffixes that keep variants side by side: `_ens...` = ensemble version, `_germany` = Germany-only copy, `uncertainty_<tag>` = a separate uncertainty run. Tags in use: `honest2` (BRT-only), `ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn` (big 5), `timing` (cheap test). |
| Seeds | `stableSeed(key)` turns a text key (species, scale, purpose) into a deterministic integer, so results do not depend on run order. |
| Entry points | Local: `source("runMe.R")` (all four modules through `SpaDES.core::simInitAndSpades`). Cluster: `cluster/*.sbatch` and `cluster/submit_eve_*.sh`, calling `runMe.R` (stages `prep`, `index`), `tools/runClusterTask.R` (model arrays), `tools/runUncertaintyTask.R`, `tools/runEnsembleTask.R`. `runMe.R` does NOT run the uncertainty workflow. |

## 1. The four modules

SpaDES loads them in the order dataPrep\_Monitor, inputs\_Monitor, models\_Monitor, runIndex\_Monitor. Stage selection (`tools/sharedStageConfig.R`): `BIRDMONITOR_STAGE` = `all`, `prep` (modules 1 and 2), `rasters` (module 1, rasters only) or `index` (module 4). All four use `timeunit = "year"` as a formality: events run at `time(sim)`.

### 1.1 dataPrep\_Monitor

**Purpose.** Builds every predictor raster (climate, elevation/slope/solar radiation, land use, land cover, two derived layers) and the per-species occurrence tables of the three scales. It is the only module that downloads anything (predictor rasters only); raw bird survey data must already be in `inputs/response/raw/`.

| Event | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | `warmUpSfProj()` (sf must initialise GDAL/PROJ before terra), checks `species`, schedules the events below. |
| `prepareClimateData` | CHELSA monthly data to bioclim rolling-window climatologies (6-year windows) for each target year, at 50 km. |
| `prepareDEM` | Copernicus GLO-30 DEM to elevation, slope, solar radiation. |
| `prepareLanduse` | Crop-type maps per year and resolution. |
| `prepareLandcover` | CORINE land cover (CLMS API; needs your own token JSON) for 2006/2012/2018. |
| `prepareDerivedCovariates` | `dist_to_woodland` and `landscape_heterogeneity`, built from the two events above. |
| `prepareOccurrenceData` | EBBA2 (Europe), MhB point counts (habitat, and landscape for species routed to MhB) and DDA territories (landscape default) to per-species, per-year presence/absence tables with the covariates attached; spatial thinning. |

**Key parameters.** `targetCRS` EPSG:3035; `europeBbox` (72, -25, 34, 45); resolutions 50000/200/1000 m; `climateTargetYears` 2005:2025 and `climateWindowLength` 6; `ebba2TrainingYear` 2017 (window 2012-2017 trains the European climate model); `landuseYears` 2005:2025; `species` and `germanNames` (DDA data has no Latin names); thinning at 2 x resolution (`useSpatialThinning`, `thinDist*M`, per-species overrides); the `rerun*` switches force a step even if its output exists; `rastersOnly`; `clmsTokenJSONPath` (keep outside git).

**Reads** `inputs/response/raw/{ornitho,MhB,territories}/` and remote CHELSA and CLMS/Copernicus. **Writes** `inputs/predictors/raw/...` (monthly CHELSA files from daily data use `<var>_<year>_<month>_dmean.tif` since 2026-10-07, old caches are never reused), `inputs/predictors/processed/<scale label>/` (bioclim windows, land use, land cover, elevation, slope, solar radiation, the two derived layers) and `inputs/response/processed/{ornitho,MhB,territories}/<Species>_...rds`.

**Coordinate safety (since 2026-10-05).** On EVE, `sf::st_transform(., 3035)` returned x and y swapped when terra had touched GDAL first. Three safeguards: `warmUpSfProj()`, `transformToLAEA()` (validates each library transform against a closed-form formula and falls back to it), `laeaCoordinates()` (stops if the points look swapped). `occurrenceCacheSchema` (currently 4) is part of the cache key so tables built before a fix are never reused.

**Study area, complete layers and cache keys (since 20 and 21 October).** `studyArea.R` (identical copies in `dataPrep_Monitor`, `models_Monitor` and `runIndex_Monitor`; `tools/check_duplicated_functions.R` compares them) builds the study area from one specification and, in `applyStudyAreaToProcessed()`, crops and masks the processed layers in place, leaving a `.studyarea` stamp file next to each layer. A second pass with the same area changes nothing; a layer cropped for a smaller area is refused for a larger one. The climate training window (Europe) is never cropped. `completeHedges()` fills the hedge layer of every land-use file without hedge data from the nearest preceding year with data (years before the first use the first), and `checkNoNAInsideStudyArea()` stops the run if any processed layer has NA inside the area. Land cover has 7 CORINE classes plus `unmapped_other`; `landscape_heterogeneity` is version 2. Occurrence tables are extracted from, and cached on, only the layers a species uses. Tests: `modules/dataPrep_Monitor/tests/test_studyArea.R` (13 checks) and `test_completeHedges.R`.

### 1.2 inputs\_Monitor

**Purpose.** Pools the occurrence tables across years, builds spatial cross-validation blocks, selects predictors and writes the model-ready table of every species and scale. No commit since 2026-10-05.

| Event | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `spatialBlocking` | Pools the per-year files (restricted to each species' own fitting years), then real `blockCV::cv_spatial()` blocks per scale, grouped by each species' resolution (own reference grid and block-size floor each), or `mimicSpatialBlocks()` (random folds, same structure) if `runSpatialBlocking = FALSE`. |
| `collinearityCheck` | Candidate predictors come ONLY from `speciesPredictorTable` (`data/speciesConfig_predictors.csv`; a species missing there is a hard error). If `dropCollinearPredictors = TRUE` the list is pruned by `select07Blockcv()`. Optional x/y coordinates are added per species and scale. Writes the model-ready files. |

**Key parameters.** `kFolds` 5; block size cap and floor (climate 1,500,000 and 200,000 m; habitat and landscape cap 200,000 m; floor = `blockSizeFloorMultiplier` 2 x resolution); `collinearityThreshold` 0.7; `dropCollinearPredictors` FALSE. **Writes** `inputs/model_ready/<scale label>/<Species>_inputs.rds` (ID, coordinates, `occurrence`, `x`, `y`, `foldID`, `year`, predictors) and `<Species>_predictors.rds`, always under the SHARED resolution label of each scale. In cluster tasks the model code reads these files directly (`tools/runClusterTask.R`, `uncTrainingTable()`).

### 1.3 models\_Monitor

**Purpose.** Fits one BRT per species and scale with spatial block cross-validation, predicts every scale for all years, and combines the three predictions with a non-negative ridge logistic meta-model on the 200 m reference grid. It also hosts two optional workflows selected with `runScale`: the multi-algorithm **ensemble** (GLM, GAM, random forest, neural network, with the BRT as a member) and the **uncertainty** workflow (spatial-block bootstrap).

| Baseline event | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `modelEurope` | Per species: `gbm.step` BRT on the EBBA2 table (learning-rate search), block-CV performance, predictions for all years. Has a content-based cache key (md5 of the climatology) so a rebuilt climate window never hits an old cache. |
| `modelGerHabitat` | The same at 200 m. Covariate stacks are loaded one year at a time; `habitatYearChunk` splits the years over several R processes to reset memory. |
| `modelGerLandscape` | The same at the landscape resolution. |
| `metaModel` | Per species: extracts the three scale predictions at the habitat records, fits the ridge (weights >= 0, penalty `lambda.1se` of 10-fold CV) and predicts all years on the 200 m grid. With `metaHonestEval = TRUE` (default) the weights and the reported accuracy use OUT-OF-FOLD inputs. |

In cluster mode only one event is scheduled per task; whichever scale finishes last for a species triggers `metaModel` (`checkAllScalesReady()`), and for the habitat array only the last year chunk may do so.

**Uncertainty events** (one at a time through `runScale`): `uncertaintyCovcache`, `uncertaintyFit`, `uncertaintyCoarse`, `uncertaintyOof`, `uncertaintyRidge`, `uncertaintyBand`, `uncertaintySummarize`, `uncertaintyAssemble`, `uncertaintyCommunity` (all through `uncHandleEvent()`). The regional, ridge-redo and mask steps are not SpaDES events: `tools/runUncertaintyTask.R` calls their functions directly.

**Key parameters.** Baseline: `predictionYears`, `habitatYears`, resolutions, `scalesToRun`, `*InitialLR` (0.01, 0.08, 0.08), `runScale`/`runSpecies`/`runBand`, `rerun*`, `habitatYearChunk`, `metaScaleSource` (`brt` or an ensemble name), `metaHonestEval` (TRUE). Uncertainty: `uncertaintyReps` (NULL = off; 0 = main models, a parity check, never in an interval; top-up runs need disjoint ids such as 51:100), `uncertaintyBands` (16; 48 for the big 5), `uncertaintyRepBatch` 10, `uncertaintyBlockMult` 1, `uncertaintyProbs` (0.05, 0.95), `uncertaintyTag`, `uncertaintyMembers` (NA = BRT-only; else a subset of brt, glm, gam, rf, nn averaged inside every replicate), `uncertaintyBaselineYear` 2005.

**Writes** `<scale label>/`, `metamodel_<label>[_<tag>]/`, `uncertainty[_<tag>]/` (section 3 of this page). runIndex\_Monitor reads `metamodel_<label>[_<tag>]/<Species>_meta_suitability_<year>.tif` (band `meta_prob` = probability, band `binary` = thresholded).

### 1.4 runIndex\_Monitor

**Purpose.** From the finished meta-model maps: species indices, four combined multi-species indices (the Analytical one is computed by the code but no longer reported, see the Consortium decisions), a richness map, change maps and regional gridded indices. No model fitting. It also turns the uncertainty run into intervals.

| Event | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | Checks `species`, `allYears`, `currentYear`. With `uncertaintyOnly = TRUE` it schedules only `computeIndexUncertainty`. |
| `checkAllInputs` | Polls until every species has meta-model output for `currentYear` (needed only for cluster runs); warns and proceeds after `pollTimeoutHours`. |
| `computeIndices` | Optionally selects the best meta-model per species across runs; fetches the GADM Germany outline; runs `computeAnnualReport()` then `computeRegionalIndex()`. |
| `computeIndexUncertainty` | Intervals for species and combined indices; stitches the community maps. |

**Key parameters.** `baselineYear` 2005; `outputTag` (reads `metamodel_<label>_<tag>`, writes `annual_report_<tag>` and `regional_index_<tag>`; `germany` and ensemble names are used this way); `changeThresh` 0.05 (change in probability counted as increase/decrease); `nBoot` 999 and `nSim` 1000 (bootstrap reps for SBI and Chain; Monte Carlo sims for MSI); `cellSizesM` 10/20/50 km; `uncertaintyDir`, `uncertaintyOnly`, `uncertaintyAreaMeanFile` (`area_mean_replicates.csv` or `area_mean_replicates_germany.csv`).

### 1.5 End-to-end data flow

1. **Raw data to predictors and occurrence tables** (dataPrep): EBBA2, MhB and DDA surveys plus CHELSA, DEM, land use and CORINE become rasters on three grids in EPSG:3035 and per-species, per-year occurrence tables with covariates.
2. **Model-ready tables** (inputs): pool years, spatial CV blocks (`foldID`), choose predictors.
3. **Three scale models** (models): a BRT per species and scale; block-CV performance; maps for every year (bands `mean_prob`, `binary`). Optionally GLM, GAM, RF and NN on the same predictors and folds, averaged into an ensemble per scale.
4. **Meta-model** (models): out-of-fold predictions of the three scales at the habitat records train a non-negative ridge logistic regression; applied to the three maps (bilinearly resampled to the 200 m grid) it gives `<Species>_meta_suitability_<year>.tif`. This map is the pipeline's product.
5. **Indices** (runIndex): area mean of `meta_prob` per species and year gives the species index (100 x mean / baseline mean), then SBI, MSI (the Monte Carlo step of Soldaat et al. 2017; the DDA's exclusions and truncation of low values are not implemented) and Chain, plus the Analytical index (PECBMS-style delta method), which the code still computes but which is no longer reported; richness map; change maps (probability change, gain/loss, stable/increase/decrease, community layers including Bray-Curtis turnover); regional gridded index (geometric mean over species of the cell index).
6. **Uncertainty** (separate workflow): replicate 0 = main models (parity check). Replicates 1 to B: block-bootstrap the training rows of each scale, refit each scale's BRT with the main model's fixed hyperparameters (and, in an ensemble run, the other members on the same draw), out-of-fold inputs per replicate, replicate ridge, predict all years in bands, summarise across replicates (percentile maps, change, per-pixel trend, share decreasing/increasing). Area means per replicate give the index intervals; per-replicate cell means of German pixels give the regional index with uncertainty. Everything derived is computed inside each replicate before the percentiles are taken.

On top: Germany-only copies (the prediction window is the bounding box of Germany; 7 of 11 species were predicted across the whole window, 4 only inside Germany) and ensemble versions with tag `ens...`.

### 1.6 connector\_Monitor (new, 20 October; not run by `runMe.R`)

**Purpose.** Keeps ONE folder, the viz folder (`/data/birds/viz` on EVE), that always holds the newest result of every species and every layer the Monitor shows. It fits and predicts nothing. For each result it takes the newest source file from all run folders (`vizSources()`, `vizLatest()`), so a species that was updated in a later run replaces the older one and a species that was not touched keeps its file. It never deletes anything, replaces a file only by a newer one, and splits every multilayer raster into one file per layer. It writes `_manifest.csv` (every file, its source, run and time) and `_missing.csv` (what the Monitor expects and the folder does not have).

| Folder in the viz folder | File | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta_prob_year/<Species>/` | `<Species>_<year>.tif` | probability of occurrence (the `meta_prob` layer only) |
| `meta_unc_year/<Species>/` | `<Species>_<year>_<layer>.tif` | uncertainty; layer = mean, sd, lwr, upr, width |
| `richness_year/` | `richness_<year>_<layer>.tif` | expected richness and its uncertainty, every year |
| `msi_regional/` | `msi_10km_<year>.tif` | regional index (10 km), raw |
| `msi_regional_unc/` | `msi_10km_<year>_<layer>.tif` | its uncertainty |
| `msi_national/` | `msi_national.csv` | national trend: method, year, estimate, median, lwr, upr, `preliminary` (TRUE for the years after the last published national indicator year) |

The first three folders follow the Confluence page "EVE Cluster" (section "Data structure", version of 19 October); the other three names are ours until agreed. The page describes the uncertainty file with 5 layers; the project lead decided on 28 October to write one raster per metric. The connector reads the ensemble folders (`metamodel_<res>_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany`, `uncertainty_<tag>`, `regional_index_<tag>_germany`, `annual_report_<tag>_germany`). It is run with `tools/runConnector.R` (on EVE `sbatch cluster/eve_connector.sbatch`; `BIRDMONITOR_VIZ_DRY=1` only reports). The cut-off year of the preliminary national trend is `sharedNationalIndicatorLastYear` (2023 for now, to be confirmed with the DDA contact) or `BIRDMONITOR_NATIONAL_LAST_YEAR`; the connector applies it, so changing it needs no new model run. Test: `Rscript modules/connector_Monitor/tests/test_connector.R` (22 checks, synthetic data).

## 2. Output file map

`<run>` = `outputs/<runName>/`, `<Sp>` = species with underscores, `<label>` = scale label, `<tag>` = variant tag.

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `<run>/scale_50/` (climate), `scale_1/` (landscape), `scale_02/` (habitat) | Per species: `<Sp>_BRT_{EU,landscape,habitat}.rds` (main BRT), `<Sp>_perf_*.rds` (block-CV performance), `<Sp>_foldModels_*.rds` (BRT per CV fold, used for the out-of-fold meta inputs), `<Sp>_expl_dev_*.rds`, `<Sp>_converged_lr_*.rds`, prediction maps `<Sp>_pred_{EU,landscape,habitat}_<year>.tif` (bands `mean_prob`, `binary`). Ensemble extras in the same folder: `<Sp>_{glm,gam,rf,nn}_<scale>.rds`, `_perf_`, `_cvpred_`, `_oofhab_` and `_pred_<algo>_<scale>_<year>.tif` files, and per ensemble tag the averaged versions plus `_sd_` (spread across members). |
| `<run>/metamodel_02_1_50[_<tag>]/` | Per species: `<Sp>_meta_suitability_<year>.tif` (bands `meta_prob`, `binary`), `<Sp>_ridge_meta.rds` (model, `lambda`), `<Sp>_perf_meta.rds` (out-of-fold accuracy), `<Sp>_perf_meta_inSample.rds` (old optimistic number, never quote), `<Sp>_meta_check.rds`, `<Sp>_varimp_meta.rds` (importance of the three scales), `<Sp>_meta_ridgeid.txt` (which weights made the maps; a mismatch rebuilds every year). |
| `<run>/metamodel_02_1_50[_<tag>]_germany/` | Germany-only copies of the suitability maps (`tools/maskMetaModels.R`), values outside the outline NA. |
| `<run>/annual_report[_<tag>][_germany]/` | `species_index.csv`, `combined_index_{sbi,analytical,msi,chain}.csv`, `SR_map_<currentYear>.tif`, change maps (`change_<comp>_community.tif` with 5 layers: meanDeltaP, netGainLoss, gainCount, lossCount, turnoverBC; per species 3 layers: deltaP, gainLoss, stableIncDec), and from the uncertainty step `species_index_uncertainty.csv` and `combined_index_uncertainty.csv` (method = SBI, Chain, Analytical, MSI; year, nReplicates, estimate, median, lwr, upr). |
| `<run>/regional_index[_<tag>][_germany]/` | `regional_index_<km>km_raw.tif` and `_smoothed.tif`, km = 10, 20, 50, one layer per year. |
| `<run>/meta_check/`, `performance_table.csv` | Output of `tools/runMetaCheck.R` and `tools/collectPerformance.R`. |

**Uncertainty folder `<run>/uncertainty_<tag>/`, per species `<Sp>/`:**

| Sub-folder or file | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `models/` | `<scale>_<runlabel>.rds` (replicate BRTs, bootstrap draws, tree counts, block size; replicate 0 = main BRT); in ensemble runs also `<scale>_<member>_<runlabel>.rds` and, if any refit failed, `refit_fallbacks.csv` (replicates where the main fit stood in). |
| `coarse/<runlabel>/` | `climate_<year>.tif`, `landscape_<year>.tif`, one layer per replicate. |
| `oof/` | `oof_<runlabel>.rds` (out-of-fold inputs of every replicate; the honest inputs of the replicate ridge) and, since 2026-10-12, one checkpoint `oof_<runlabel>_<scale>.part.rds` per scale. |
| `ridge/` | `ridge_<runlabel>.rds`: coefficients per replicate (intercept, climate, landscape, habitat) and an info table (penalty, seed, note). |
| `pred/<runlabel>/` | `<year>_band<NN>.rds`: 16-bit packed probabilities of the valid cells of one band for all replicates; `stats_*`: per-replicate sums. Large (about 8-12 GB per species per UNCERTAINTY.md); they allow adding replicates later. |
| `pieces/`, `maps/` | Band pieces, then stitched maps: `<Sp>_unc_<year>.tif` (mean, sd, lwr, upr, width), `<Sp>_unc_change_<comp>.tif` (delta mean/sd/lwr/upr/width plus shareDecrease and shareIncrease), `<Sp>_unc_trend_per_decade.tif` (slope layers, same structure). `<comp>` = vsBaseline, vs5YearsAgo, vsLastYear. `maps_germany/` = the same cut to the German outline. |
| `regional/` | Partial sums per coarse cell (`regionband`) and `regional_means_<km>km.rds`. |
| `area_mean_replicates.csv`, `area_mean_replicates_germany.csv` | Country area mean per replicate and year, over all valid pixels of the window / over German pixels only. |
| `parity_check.txt`, `replicate_log.csv`, `blocksize.rds`, `run_info_<runlabel>.txt` | Replicate 0 vs baseline (`RESULT: OK` or `MISMATCH`); one row per fitted BRT (seeds, attempts, hyperparameters, git hashes); resampling block size; session info. |

**Across species** (`uncertainty_<tag>/`): `covcache/` (habitat covariate stacks, always under `<run>/uncertainty/covcache/`, shared by all tags), `combined_index_replicates.csv` (SBI and Chain per replicate and year), `community/` (`richness_expected_unc_<year>.tif`, `community_meanDeltaP_unc_<comp>.tif`, `community_turnoverBC_unc_<comp>.tif`) and `community_germany/`, `regional/` (`regional_index_<km>km_unc_<year>.tif`, `..._unc_change_<comp>.tif`, `..._unc_trend_per_decade.tif`, `..._coverage.tif`, `..._replicates.rds`, `regional_parity_<km>km.txt`), and `_old_ridge_blockfolds_2026-10-10/` (the earlier results made with the block-fold penalty, kept as the sensitivity analysis).

## 3. Things not verified, and documentation that disagrees with the code

1. **Stale comment in `uncBand.R`.** The docstring above `uncRidgeSpecies` still says replicates use spatial-block folds for the penalty; the code (since 2026-10-10) uses ten random folds unless `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_RIDGEFOLDS=block`.
2. **`UNCERTAINTY.md`** writes `outputs/<runName>/uncertainty/` throughout; the code writes `uncertainty_<tag>/` when a tag is set (always for ensemble runs), and the document does not mention the penalty rule, regional, maskmaps or ridgeredo.
3. **`README.md`** still says the workflow has never been submitted to the cluster and names a feature branch; all repos are on `main`, runs have happened. It does not describe the ensemble, uncertainty, Germany-only or regional products.
4. **Event order.** dataPrep and runIndex rely on SpaDES running same-time events in scheduling order (read from comments, not from the SpaDES source).
5. **`blockCVPredictAlgo`** is called only by a test script; `algoScaleRun` has its own fold loop.
6. **Floors.** `minBaseline = 1e-6` is set in two places (baseline `computeGriddedCombinedIndex` and the `regionindex` step); if the floor/cap decision changes, change both.
7. **Axis robustness differs.** `aggregateSpeciesToGrid()` (baseline regional index) still projects the outline with `terra::project`; the uncertainty and masking code use the closed-form outline. It would fail loudly with a crop error, not give wrong numbers.
8. **Not read in detail:** `runClusterTask.R` beyond its header, config-parsing helpers, runIndex helper functions (none changed since 5 October), inputs\_Monitor and most dataPrep implementation files, the unit tests.
9. **(29 October) The connector has never run on real results**, only on synthetic files. The first real run is the end of the clean run.
10. **(29 October) Richness for every year** is a change in the community step (`uncCommunityBand`) that has been parsed and unit-tested but not run on real replicate data; it reads the replicates of all species once per year, so the step is slower than before (not measured).
11. **(29 October) The cut-off year of the preliminary national trend (2023)** is a placeholder to confirm with the DDA contact; the figure code that draws the dashed line is not written.
12. **(29 October) The upload from `/data/birds/viz` to the bucket** is not in this repository; how it is done and who does it is not recorded here.
13. **(29 October) Falco tinnunculus uses a provisional full predictor set** copied from Passer montanus; its small-woodlot habitat is not resolved by the layers (decision to judge it from its maps).
14. **(29 October) Saxony test:** only the preparation stage was tested for a smaller study area; nothing downstream (models, index) has run on a study area other than Germany.


# 4. Glossary of functions and scripts

Every script and function written or changed since 2026-10-05 (when the cluster work began). Part A = cluster scripts and tools (this page, sections A1 to A6). Part B = the R functions of the modules (sections B1 onwards). "Reusable" = takes its settings from arguments or environment variables. "One-off" = tied to a dated incident or to hard-coded job ids: use it as a template, do not run it again. Read from the files, not run again for this document; where a file does not say, the text says "unclear".

**Conventions in all commands.** `~/projects/birdMonitor` is the repo root on EVE; always `cd` there first. `<run>` = baseline run folder = `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` (default `test4`; use the same value in every step). `<tag>` = uncertainty run tag (`BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG`): the BRT-only run is `honest2`, the big 5 run is `ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn`. Species count: 11 until 21 October, 14 since 28 October; the array jobs follow the roster size since 21 October (older scripts and this page's older rows may still say 11). Replicate label in file names: `reps_000-050` for replicates 0 to 50.

## A1. Submit and setup scripts (run on a login node; they call `sbatch`)

| Name | What it does | How to run | Settings and outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cluster/setup_uncertainty.sh` | Installs the extra R packages of the uncertainty workflow and of the algorithm ensemble (matrixStats, ranger, nnet, mgcv, geodata) into the personal R library and prints the version of each (or MISSING). Stops if the birdMonitor library is missing ("run cluster/setup\_eve.sh first"). | `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor && bash --login cluster/setup_uncertainty.sh` | `EVE_R_MODULE` (default `GCC/13.3.0 OpenMPI/5.0.5 R/4.5.1 GDAL/3.10.3 CMake ImageMagick/7.1.1-38 UDUNITS/2.2.28`). Reusable, idempotent. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_pipeline.sh` | Baseline workflow: prep, then three model arrays (europe, habitat, landscape; the meta-model starts by itself), then index. No double-submission guard. Does not submit `eve_covcache.sbatch` (see the run guide). | `bash cluster/submit_eve_pipeline.sh` | `EVE_R_MODULE`, `EVE_PARTITION`, `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_germany_baseline.sh` | Baseline index on Germany-only maps: `eve_mask_meta.sbatch` (array over species), then `eve_index.sbatch` with `BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG=germany`. The rectangle versions stay untouched so both can be compared. Has the guard. | `bash --login cluster/submit_eve_germany_baseline.sh` (`FORCE=1` overrides the guard) | Results: `metamodel_<res>_germany/`, `annual_report_germany/`, `regional_index_germany/`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_uncertainty.sh` | The whole BRT-only uncertainty chain (spatial-block bootstrap): preflight (login node), covcache, prepare (per species), band (species x band), summarize, assemble + community, assembleall. `--dependency=afterok` and `--kill-on-invalid-dep` throughout. Rerun with the SAME settings after a failure: finished work is skipped. No guard. | `bash --login cluster/submit_eve_uncertainty.sh` | `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS` (default `0:50`; `51:100` adds replicates later), `_YEARS`, `_BANDS` (16), `_BLOCKMULT`, `_TAG`, `_MEMBERS`; `UNC_THROTTLE`; `UNC_AFTER` (job ids to wait for); `UNC_BAND_TIME` (default 12 h); `UNC_PREP_TIME`; `UNC_PREPARE_JOB` (reuse a prepare job). Results in `outputs/<run>/uncertainty[_<tag>]/`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_regional.sh` | Regional-index chain (10/20/50 km): regionband, regionassemble, regionindex, then assembleAll again with the German-only area means, then maskmaps (12 tasks). Reads the stored replicate predictions; nothing is refitted. Has the guard. | `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG=honest2 UNC_AFTER=<band id> bash --login cluster/submit_eve_regional.sh` | `UNC_FINAL` = the main chain's assembleall id (the German-only assembleAll waits for it so the two never write at once), `UNC_THROTTLE`, `FORCE=1`. Results in `<uncertainty folder>/regional/`, `maps_germany/`, `community_germany/`, `annual_report_germany/`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_ensemble.sh` | Algorithm ensemble ("big 5"): fit (array per scale x algorithm; BRT is not refitted), ensemble means per scale, meta-model (`BIRDMONITOR_META_SOURCE=<ensTag>`), index. Resources per task are set in the script (habitat rf 4 cpu x 8G 12 h; habitat other 1 x 12G 12 h; landscape rf 4 x 4G 6 h, other 1 x 8G 6 h; climate rf 2 x 4G 3 h, other 1 x 8G 3 h). No guard. | `ENS_ALGOS="glm gam rf nn" ENS_VARIANTS="brt,glm,gam,rf,nn" ENS_THROTTLE=11 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_ensemble.sh` | `ENS_ALGOS`, `ENS_VARIANTS` (member sets separated by `;`), `ENS_SCALES`, `ENS_AFTER`, `ENS_THROTTLE`. Tag: `ens` for brt,glm,gam,rf; otherwise `ens_<members joined by ->`. Prints `meta <tag>: <jobid>`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_ensemble_uncertainty.sh` | The uncertainty chain with the ensemble inside every replicate; sets members, 48 bands, throttle 100, then calls `submit_eve_uncertainty.sh`. Needs the members fitted, the baseline ensemble and its meta-model, and the habitat covariate cache. | `ENS_MEMBERS=brt,glm,gam,rf,nn BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=0:25 UNC_BAND_TIME=24:00:00 UNC_PREP_TIME=24:00:00 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_ensemble_uncertainty.sh` | `ENS_MEMBERS`, `ENS_BANDS`, plus the settings of the uncertainty script. Folder `uncertainty_<ensTag>/`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_big5_uncertainty.sh` | The big 5 uncertainty chain in one command: the script above with 25 replicates, then the regional steps behind it. Guard on all `unc-*` jobs. | `bash --login cluster/submit_eve_big5_uncertainty.sh` | `BIG5_REPS` (0:25), `BIG5_PREP_TIME`, `FORCE`. Reusable (big 5 settings hard-coded). Does not set the prepare memory: see the run guide. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` | **The entry point of the clean run (run folder `v2`), written 21 October.** One command chains: checks, preparation, the BRT arrays at three scales, the ensemble (GLM, GAM, RF, NN fits, means, honest meta-model), the reporting-area copies and the index, the uncertainty (25 replicates inside the ensemble), the regional steps, the copy to `/data/birds` and the connector. Checks before anything is submitted: no `BIRDMONITOR_SPECIES` or `BIRDMONITOR_YEARS` set; `outputs/<run>` does not exist (`RESUME=1` overrides); clean git state and modules at their pinned commits; a complete safety copy of `inputs/predictors/processed` and `inputs/response/processed` in `/data/birds/birdMonitor/inputs` (`SKIP_BACKUP_CHECK=1` overrides); identical duplicated functions; the EBBA2 file exists (its name, checksum, size, rows and species count are printed and written to `outputs/<run>/RUN_INFO.txt`); `tools/checkSpeciesData.R` finds every roster species ready; the study area builds. | `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor && git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive && bash --login cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` (`DRY_RUN=1` prints the chain without submitting) | `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` (default `v2`), `DATA_BIRDS_INPUTS`. Prints every job id. Reusable. About 2 days. |
| `cluster/eve_copy_data_birds.sbatch` (and `cluster/copy_to_data_birds.sh`) | Copies `inputs/`, `outputs/<run>` and `logs/` to `/data/birds/birdMonitor` with rsync (adds and updates, never deletes; `pieces/`, `covcache/` and by default `pred/` are left out). `MODE=sizes`, `MODE=dry` and `MODE=verify` only read; `MODE=verify` lists every file that differs. | `sbatch cluster/eve_copy_data_birds.sbatch`; check: `COPY_INPUTS=1 MODE=verify bash cluster/copy_to_data_birds.sh` | `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` (default `test4`), `COPY_INPUTS`, `COPY_PRED`, `DEST`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/eve_connector.sbatch` | Runs `tools/runConnector.R`: fills `/data/birds/viz` with the newest result of every species and layer. | `sbatch cluster/eve_connector.sbatch` (`BIRDMONITOR_VIZ_DRY=1` only reports) | `BIRDMONITOR_VIZ_PATH`, `_RUNS_ROOT`, `_VIZ_RUNS`, `_VIZ_TAG`, `BIRDMONITOR_NATIONAL_LAST_YEAR`. Reusable. |
| `cluster/submit_eve_tonight.sh` | Everything queued in one go on 2026-10-08. | not to be run again | **One-off.** Its big 5 baseline part (ensemble means, meta, index, Germany copy) exists nowhere else as a script; the run guide has the two commands. |

## A2. SLURM job scripts (submitted by the scripts above; do not submit by hand unless you know the dependencies)

| Name (job name) | What it does and resources | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cluster/eve_unc_common.sh` | Sourced by every `eve_unc_*`, `eve_ens_*` and similar job. Loads the modules, sets `TMPDIR=/work/$USER/birdMonitor/tmp/<jobid>_<task>` (EVE's TMPDIR is a RAM disk) with cleanup, `BIRDMONITOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1`, and defines `unc_run`: if a task fails with a nonzero code but wrote its done-marker (the last act of the R script), it counts as success (R/terra segmentation fault at exit, code 139, seen 2026-10-07). | The `.err` file says "NOTE: ... exited with code N AFTER finishing its work" when this rescued a task. |
| `eve_unc_covcache.sbatch` (`unc-covcache`) | Preflight, then the 200 m habitat covariate stack of every needed year (1-2 min per year); skips if files exist. 1 cpu x 16G, 8 h. | `outputs/<run>/uncertainty/covcache/scale_02/habitat_<year>.tif`, shared by all tags |
| `eve_unc_prepare.sbatch` (`unc-prepare`) | Per species (array 1-11): steps fit (replicate BRTs), coarse (climate/landscape predictions), oof (out-of-fold inputs), ridge (replicate ridge models). 8 cpu x 8G = 64 GB, 10 h by default. The big 5 needs 128 GB (`--mem-per-cpu=16G`) and 24 h or more. | `<unc>/<species>/models/`, `coarse/`, `oof/`, `ridge/` |
| `eve_unc_band.sbatch` (`unc-band`) | Per species x band: predict all years for all replicates (the expensive part). 4 cpu x 13G, 12 h by default (24 h for the big 5). | `<unc>/<species>/pred/<label>/` (16-bit integers) |
| `eve_unc_summarize.sbatch` (`unc-summarize`) | Per species x band: percentile maps, change maps, per-pixel trend. 2 x 12G, 4 h. | `<unc>/<species>/pieces/` |
| `eve_unc_assemble.sbatch` (`unc-assemble`) | Per species: stitches the pieces into maps, area means, index uncertainty, replicate-0 parity check. 1 x 16G, 4 h. | `maps/`, `area_mean_replicates.csv`, `parity_check.txt` |
| `eve_unc_community.sbatch` (`unc-community`) | Per band: expected richness, mean change and Bray-Curtis turnover over all species. 2 x 16G, 4 h. | `<unc>/community/` |
| `eve_unc_assembleall.sbatch` (`unc-assembleall`) | Once: combined multi-species indices per replicate and stitched community maps (runIndex\_Monitor in `uncertaintyOnly` mode). With `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_AREAMEAN=area_mean_replicates_germany.csv` and `BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG` it gives the Germany-only version. 1 x 16G, 2 h. | `outputs/<run>/annual_report[_<tag>][_germany]/` |
| `eve_unc_regionband.sbatch`, `eve_unc_regionassemble.sbatch`, `eve_unc_regionindex.sbatch` | Per species x band: sums of replicate predictions of the German 200 m pixels per 10/20/50 km cell (2 x 8G, 2 h); per species: add the bands up (1 x 16G, 1 h); once: regional index per replicate with intervals, change, trend, coverage and parity against the baseline (1 x 24G, 1 h). | `<unc>/regional/` incl. `regional_parity_<km>km.txt` |
| `eve_unc_maskmaps.sbatch` (`unc-maskmaps`) | Tasks 1 to 11: Germany-only copies of each species' finished uncertainty maps; task 12: community maps. 2 x 8G, 2 h. | `maps_germany/`, `community_germany/` |
| `eve_unc_ridgeredo.sbatch` (`unc-ridgeredo`) | Per species: moves the replicate ridge file to `_old_ridge_blockfolds_2026-10-10/` and recomputes it with the current penalty rule (ten random folds, as the baseline). 2 x 16G, 2 h. | new `ridge/ridge_<label>.rds`. One-off in practice (the folder name is hard-coded). |
| `eve_covcache.sbatch` (`birdmon-covcache`) | Baseline step before the habitat array: writes the 200 m habitat covariate stack of every year as GeoTIFF so the habitat array reads files instead of building each year in memory (11.6 GB peak per year, killed habitat tasks twice). 1 x 24G, 4 h. | same files the uncertainty workflow reuses |
| `eve_ens_algo.sbatch` (`ens-<scale>-<algo>`) | Fit, block-CV and predict ONE algorithm at ONE scale for one species (array 1-11). Finished years are kept, so a task that hits the time limit resumes when submitted again. | `<sp>_<algo>_<scale>.rds`, maps, out-of-fold files |
| `eve_ens_ens.sbatch` (`ens-mean`) | Averages the members' maps of one scale for one species. 1 x 12G, 4 h. | ensemble maps, ensemble block-CV performance |
| `eve_mask_meta.sbatch` (`mask-meta`) | Germany-only copies of the meta-model maps (array 1-11). 2 x 8G, 2 h. For the big 5: `MASK_META_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn`. | `metamodel_<res>[_<tag>]_germany/` |
| `eve_meta_check.sbatch` (`birdmon-metacheck`) | Honest accuracy of the combined map, one task per species; minutes each. Then `Rscript tools/runMetaCheck.R --collect`. | `outputs/<run>/meta_check/` |
| `eve_index.sbatch` (`birdmon-index`) | Final baseline stage: runIndex\_Monitor through `runMe.R` with `BIRDMONITOR_STAGE=index`. Measured 2026-10-06: 35 min, peak 20.1 GB. 4 x 8G, 12 h. Re-used with `BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG` for Germany-only and ensemble indices. | `annual_report[_<tag>]/`, `regional_index[_<tag>]/` |
| `modules/models_Monitor/cluster/eve_array_habitat.sbatch` (`birdmon-habitat`) | Fit, CV and predict the German 200 m habitat BRT, one task per species. Predicts the years in 6 separate R processes (`HABITAT_NCHUNKS`) because memory kept growing; reads the covariate cache. 1 x 12G, 12 h. | `outputs/<run>/scale_02/` |
| `modules/models_Monitor/cluster/eve_array_meta.sbatch` (`birdmon-meta`) | Normally not needed (the meta-model starts by itself). Catches stragglers, or runs the ensemble meta-model with `BIRDMONITOR_META_SOURCE=<ensTag>`. 1 x 13G, 4 h. | `metamodel_<res>[_<tag>]/` |

| `tools/diagnoseParityMaps.R` (+ wrapper) | Parity step 2: at random German pixels, the three scale maps and the final map of replicate 0 vs the baseline per year and species, with each scale's contribution to the difference. | `Rscript tools/diagnoseParityMaps.R [run] [tag] [label] [years] [species] [points]` |
| `tools/diagnoseParityModels.R` (+ wrapper) | Parity step 3: baseline main BRT vs the model stored as replicate 0: number of trees, predictions on 500 training rows, file times. Found the cause of the 9 October mismatch. | `Rscript tools/diagnoseParityModels.R [run] [tag] [label]` |
| `tools/diagnoseReplicateBias.R` (+ wrapper) | Why do the replicates show less decline than the baseline? Per species: last-year index of replicate 0 vs replicates (median, 5%, 95%, rank), ridge weights, penalty. Led to the ridge-rule decision. | `Rscript tools/diagnoseReplicateBias.R [run] [tag] [label] [year]` |
| `tools/checkRidgeParity.R` | Replicate-0 ridge weights vs the baseline meta-model's weights (`maxDiff` about 0). Default tag is `honest`, not `honest2`: pass the tag. | `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=<run> Rscript tools/checkRidgeParity.R <tag>` |
| `tools/diagnoseYearJump.R` | Why does a species' index jump in the last years? Country mean and valid cells per scale and year; replicate spread; top predictors' yearly mean and share of cells outside the training range. | `Rscript tools/diagnoseYearJump.R "Anthus pratensis,Lullula arborea" --tag <tag>` |
| `tools/diagnoseBRT.R` | Why does the BRT of one species and scale fail? The same fit as the arrays, warnings printed, for three starting learning rates. | `Rscript tools/diagnoseBRT.R "Vanellus vanellus" climate` |
| `tools/checkClimateMonthly.R`, `tools/checkClimateWindows.R` | Sanity checks of the cached monthly CHELSA rasters (the 2022 break between sources) and of the bioclim windows (exit 1 if one is missing or broken). | `Rscript tools/checkClimateMonthly.R`; `Rscript tools/checkClimateWindows.R` |
| `tools/checkGermanyShare.R` (+ `eve_check_germany_share.sbatch`) | Share of the prediction window outside Germany and the area mean with and without it. | `sbatch cluster/eve_check_germany_share.sbatch` |
| `tools/floorCounts.R` (+ `eve_floor_counts.sbatch`) | Counts regional cells affected by the baseline floor `minBaseline` = 1e-6 and what other floors would change, on the Germany-only maps. | `sbatch cluster/eve_floor_counts.sbatch` |

## A5. Tools (R entry points and result summaries)

| Name | What it does | How to run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/runUncertaintyTask.R` | Entry point for ONE task of the uncertainty workflow. Steps: preflight, covcache, fit, coarse, oof, ridge, bandpredict, summarize, assemble, community, assembleAll, regionband, regionassemble, ridgeredo, maskmaps, regionindex. Each is a SpaDES event of models\_Monitor (or runIndex\_Monitor for assembleAll and regionindex). Writes a done-marker as its very last act. | `Rscript tools/runUncertaintyTask.R --step <step> [--index N]` |
| `tools/runEnsembleTask.R` | One task of the ensemble workflow: `--step algo` (fit, CV and maps of one algorithm; `brt` only rebuilds the BRT's out-of-fold files) or `--step ens` (mean of chosen members). | `Rscript tools/runEnsembleTask.R --step algo --scale habitat --algo gam --index 5` |
| `tools/runClusterTask.R` | Entry point for one species x scale/meta task of the baseline (`--scale europe\|habitat\|landscape\|meta`, `--meta-source brt\|<ensTag>`, `--year-chunk i --n-chunks n`). The meta-model starts by itself from whichever scale finishes last. | `Rscript tools/runClusterTask.R --scale habitat --index 3 --run-name test4` |
| `tools/maskMetaModels.R` | Germany-only COPIES of the meta-model maps with the German outline (closed-form transformation, no GDAL axis problem). Temporary until the inputs are cut to the outline at source. | `Rscript tools/maskMetaModels.R --index <1..11>` |
| `tools/collectPerformance.R` | One table of block-CV performance of every species and scale plus the meta-model (quote only the honest "meta" row, never "meta (in-sample, optimistic)"). | `Rscript tools/collectPerformance.R [run]` |
| `tools/summarizeIndexUncertainty.R` | Prints species and combined index with 90% interval in 2005/2010/2015/2020/2025. It reads the NEWEST matching file under `outputs/<run>/`: check the printed `files:` list to know which tag and which Germany version you are looking at. | `Rscript tools/summarizeIndexUncertainty.R [run]` |
| `tools/runConnector.R` | Entry point of `connector_Monitor` (see tab 3, section 1.6). Reads the run folders, writes the viz folder; never deletes. | `Rscript tools/runConnector.R` (on EVE through `cluster/eve_connector.sbatch`) |
| `tools/prepareEbba2Extract.R` | Brings a NEW EBBA2 extract into the pipeline without touching the file on disk: keeps presences, renames BirdLife names that differ from the roster (`sharedEbba2NameAliases`), checks the cells against the EBBA2 grid, merges, and writes a NEW dated file plus a `.merge_report.txt`; refuses to overwrite. It prints the one line (`sharedEbba2CsvSubpath` in `tools/sharedConfig.R`) that switches the pipeline to the new file. New species add cells to the "surveyed cells" universe, so the absences of ALL species are drawn from it. | `Rscript tools/prepareEbba2Extract.R <new extract.csv> [--dry]` |
| `tools/checkSpeciesData.R` | Read-only pre-flight: for every roster species (and the candidates) the number of records at each scale; lists species that are ON but not READY. Reads the EBBA2 file named in `sharedEbba2CsvSubpath`. | `Rscript tools/checkSpeciesData.R` |
| `tools/makeResultFigures.R` (+ `cluster/eve_figures.sbatch`, `cluster/pack_downloads.sh`; called `makeStCoFigures.R` until 29 October) | Every result figure of a run (made first for the Steering Consortium meeting), by section (S3 indices, S8 richness, S9 closest comparison and so on); `--sections` and `--variants` select. The number of species in titles and captions is taken from the roster (`NSP`), since 29 October; before, "11 species" was typed into 25 texts. | `FIG_ARGS="--sections S9 --variants big5" sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_figures.sbatch` |
| `R/render_figure_reference.R` (page `pdf_export/5_Figure_reference.Rmd`, helpers `pdf_export/figure_reference_helpers.R`) | The results reference page, made on the PC at the end of a full run from the figures and tables of `outputs/<run>/figures_fullreport`. The run comes from `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` (default `test4`); the species on the page and their number are those that have results in that run, so species can be added or removed without editing the page. Output: `outputs/<run>/5_Figure_reference.html` (the small figures are embedded; the click-to-enlarge links need the folder `figures_fullreport` next to it). Only the `.Rmd` and its helper are in GitHub: the page is 24 MB and the full-size figures 204 MB, so everyone renders it locally. | `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=v2 Rscript R/render_figure_reference.R` (after downloading `figures_fullreport` from EVE) |
| `tools/naHolesCheck.R` (+ `cluster/eve_na_holes_check.sbatch`) | Counts NA pixels ("holes") in the habitat, landscape and final maps and in the covariate `landscape_heterogeneity`; read-only. | `sbatch cluster/eve_na_holes_check.sbatch` |
| `tools/rebuildClimateWindows.R` | Rebuilds the bioclim windows for 2022-2025 with the fixed aggregation. Run on the PC that holds the inputs (compute nodes have no internet). | **One-off** (7 October climate incident) |
