## Part B. Glossary of the R functions

Functions created or changed since 2026-10-05 ('Called by' was found by reading the callers, not by a full static analysis). The configuration object `cfg` (a list built by `uncCfgFromParams()`) is passed to almost everything in the uncertainty workflow: it holds the input and output roots, tag, members, species, output years, baseline and current year, resolutions, replicate ids and label, number of bands, replicate batch size, cores, block multiplier and interval probabilities.

## B1. models\_Monitor, uncertainty workflow: common helpers (`uncCommon.R`)

| Function | What it does | Called by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uncRepLabel(ids)` | Label of a replicate run, e.g. `reps_000-050`. | `uncCfgFromParams` |
| `uncWithSeed(seed, expr)` | Runs `expr` under a fixed seed and restores the caller's RNG state afterwards. | `uncRowIndex`, `uncFitSpecies`, `uncOofSpecies`, `uncRidgeSpecies` |
| `uncAttemptSeed(seed, attempt)` | Seed of the n-th redraw of a replicate. | `uncRowIndex` |
| `uncGitInfo(repoRoot)` | Short git hashes of root and the four submodules for the log. | `uncFitSpecies` |
| `uncCfgFromParams(...)` | Builds `cfg` from plain values; resolves ensemble `members` and the default tag (`ensTag`). | `uncCfgFromSim`, `metaModel`, `makeCfg()` in the task scripts, diagnose tools |
| `uncRoot(cfg)`, `uncSpDir(cfg, sp, ...)`, `uncMainDir(cfg, sp, scaleKey)` | Paths: `outputs/<run>/uncertainty[_<tag>]`, a per-species folder (created), the baseline output folder of one scale. | all unc functions |
| `uncMainModel(cfg, sp, scaleKey)` | Reads the baseline main BRT; stops if missing. | `uncFitSpecies`, `uncOofSpecies`, `uncPreflight`, diagnoseParityModels |
| `uncModelReadyDir`, `uncTrainingTable` | `inputs/model_ready/<shared scale label>/` and the `<Species>_inputs.rds` table in it. | `uncBlockSizes`, `uncFitSpecies`, `uncOofContext`, `uncRidgeSpecies`, `algoScaleRun`, `metaOutOfFoldCheck` |
| `uncCovcacheFile(cfg, sp, year)` | `outputs/<run>/uncertainty/covcache/<label>/habitat_<year>.tif` (always under `uncertainty`, shared by all tags). | `uncCovcache`, `uncBands`, `uncBandSuitability`, `ensCovStack` |
| `uncAllYears(cfg, sp)` | Output years plus the species' habitat years. | several |
| `uncBands(cfg, sp)` | Cuts the 200 m window into `nBands` horizontal bands, each a template raster. | `uncHandleEvent`, `uncParityCheck`, regional steps |
| `uncBlockIds(x, y, blockSizeM)` | Square-grid block id of every row. | `uncFitSpecies`, `uncRidgeSpecies` |
| `uncRowIndex(blockIds, occurrence, seed, minPerClass = 10, maxAttempts = 50)` | One block-bootstrap draw (blocks with replacement, all rows of a drawn block); redraws deterministically if fewer than 10 presences or absences. | `uncFitSpecies` |
| `uncFitBRT(spPa, predSel, brtM, idx)` | Refits a BRT (`gbm::gbm`) on a draw with the main model's tree count, learning rate, bag fraction and tree complexity. | `uncFitSpecies`, `uncOofSpecies` |
| `uncPredictMany`, `uncPredictFits`, `uncPredictScale` | Predict many gbm models or algorithm fits on one data frame (forked); `uncPredictScale` = BRT alone (default) or the mean of the run's members. | coarse and band steps |
| `uncCells`, `uncNeighbourCells`, `uncNearestIdx` | Complete-case cells of a covariate stack; cells within 2 rows/columns (what bilinear resampling needs); nearest reference point per query point. | coarse, band, oof |
| `uncMemberFits(cfg, sp, scale, member)` | Reads and caches the replicate fits of a non-BRT member. | `uncPredictScale` |

## B2. models\_Monitor, uncertainty workflow: the steps

| Function (file) | What it does | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uncBlockSizes(cfg, sp)` (`uncFit.R`) | Resampling block size per scale from `determineBlockSize()` (autocorrelation range; climate 200-1500 km; landscape/habitat floor 2 x resolution, cap 200 km), cached in `blocksize.rds`. | `blocksize.rds` |
| `uncFitSpecies(cfg, sp)` (`uncFit.R`), step `fit` | Per scale: block-bootstrap draw per replicate, refit the BRT; replicate 0 is the main model. Fits the other members if any. | `models/<scale>_<run>.rds`, `replicate_log.csv` |
| `uncFitMembers(cfg, sp)` (`uncFit.R`) | Refits glm/gam/rf/nn on the SAME draws as the BRT replicates. An error in one refit makes the main fit stand in and is logged (since 2026-10-09). | `models/<scale>_<member>_<run>.rds`, `refit_fallbacks.csv` |
| `uncCovcache(cfg)` (`uncFit.R`), step `covcache` | Writes the 200 m habitat covariate stack of every needed year once. | `covcache/<label>/habitat_<year>.tif` |
| `uncCoarseSpecies(cfg, sp)` (`uncFit.R`), step `coarse` | Predicts the replicate climate and landscape models for all years on their own grids (cheap). | `coarse/<run>/*.tif` |
| `uncOofContext`, `uncOofCells`, `uncOofPredictFold` (`uncOof.R`) | The replicate-independent pieces of the out-of-fold step: habitat records of the habitat years and their folds, coarse covariates near the fold's records, prediction of one fold's records with one fold model. | (used by the next) |
| `uncOofSpecies(cfg, sp)` (`uncOof.R`), step `oof` | For every replicate and scale, refits fold models on (replicate draw minus fold k) and predicts the held-out habitat records; replicate 0 uses the saved fold models of the main BRT; in ensemble runs the member predictions are averaged. These are the honest inputs of the replicate ridge. **Since 2026-10-12 it saves a checkpoint per scale**, so a task that hits its time limit resumes at the first unfinished scale (Emberiza calandra timed out here). | `oof/oof_<run>.rds` (+ `oof_<run>_<scale>.part.rds`) |
| `uncRidgeSpecies(cfg, sp)` (`uncBand.R`), step `ridge` | Fits the ridge of every replicate on that replicate's out-of-fold inputs and habitat draw. **Penalty rule since 2026-10-10: the same as the baseline** (10 random folds, `lambda.1se`, via `fitRidgeCv`); `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_RIDGEFOLDS=block` restores the older spatial-block folds. Replicates with fewer than 10 presences or absences are dropped. | `ridge/ridge_<run>.rds` |
| `uncContext`, `uncBandSuitability`, `uncApplyRidge` (`uncBand.R`) | Loads the replicate models once per task; for a band and year resamples the coarse predictions bilinearly to the 200 m template and predicts the habitat model (the same as the baseline `loadSuitability`); applies `plogis(intercept + w_clim*clim + w_land*land + w_hab*hab)` per replicate. |  |
| `uncPredictBandYear(cfg, sp, ctx, ridge, year, band)` (`uncBand.R`), step `bandpredict` | Predicts all usable replicates in batches of `repBatch`, stores 16-bit integer predictions and per-replicate sums and counts; skips if both files exist. | `pred/<run>/<year>_bandNN.rds`, `stats_*` |
| `uncWriteInt16` / `uncReadInt16`, `uncSaveRDS` | Packed 16-bit storage (probability x 30000, NA = -1; resolution 3.3e-5); `saveRDS` through a `.part` file then rename, so a killed job never leaves a half file. |  |
| `uncSummarizeSpeciesBand(cfg, sp, band)` (`uncSummarize.R`), step `summarize` | Per band: per-year maps (mean, sd, lwr, upr, width), change maps (late minus early inside each replicate) and the per-pixel linear trend per decade (at least 5 years). Helpers: `uncSummarizeMatrix`, `uncSummarizeChange` (adds `shareDecrease`, `shareIncrease`), `uncComparisons` (vsBaseline, vs5YearsAgo, vsLastYear), `uncReadBandYear`, `uncWritePiece`, `uncPieceStamp`. | `pieces/` |
| `uncCommunityBand(cfg, band)` (`uncSummarize.R`), step `community` | Per band, over all species: expected richness of the current year, mean change in probability, Bray-Curtis turnover, each per replicate then summarised. `uncBrayCurtis` = sum of absolute differences / sum of totals (0 = unchanged, 1 = no species in common; probabilities stand in for abundances). | `community/pieces/` |
| `uncAssembleSpecies(cfg, sp)` (`uncSummarize.R`), step `assemble` | Stitches pieces into maps (`uncStitch`), country area mean per replicate and year (`uncAreaMeans`), and runs `uncParityCheck`: replicate 0 vs the baseline meta map, flagged MISMATCH if more than 0.1% of valid cells disagree, the maximum difference exceeds 1e-3 or the relative area-mean difference exceeds 1e-3. | `maps/`, `area_mean_replicates.csv`, `parity_check.txt` |
| `uncPreflight(cfg)` (`uncPreflight.R`) | Checks R packages and that every training table, main BRT, covariate file and reference grid exists; prints up to 40 problems and stops. File existence only. |  |
| `uncCfgFromSim`, `uncHandleEvent` (`uncSim.R`) | Build `cfg` from the module parameters; dispatch one `uncertainty*` event to the functions above. |  |

## B3. models\_Monitor, regional and Germany-only (`uncRegional.R`, new 2026-10-08)

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `uncLonLatToLAEA(lon, lat)` | Closed-form lon/lat to EPSG:3035 (no GDAL/PROJ), so the axis swap on EVE cannot occur. |
| `uncOutlineLAEA(gadmDir, crs)`, `uncGermanyBoundary(cfg, crs)` | The German outline (GADM level 0) transformed with the closed form and labelled with the raster CRS; stops if outside Germany's EPSG:3035 box. |
| `uncRegionalGrid(win, bProj, cellSizeM)` | Coarse grid of one size: window cropped to the outline, aggregated by the same factor as the baseline `aggregateSpeciesToGrid`. |
| `uncRegionalBand(cfg, sp, band, ...)`, step `regionband` | For each replicate run, year and grid size: sum and count of the German 200 m pixels (masked BEFORE averaging) per coarse cell, for one band. |
| `uncRegionalAssemble(cfg, sp, ...)`, step `regionassemble` | Adds the bands to cell means (cells x years x replicates) per grid size, and the German-only national area mean per replicate and year. |
| `uncMaskMaps(cfg, sp = NULL, outline)`, step `maskmaps` | Germany-only COPIES of the finished uncertainty maps (`maps/` to `maps_germany/`, or with `sp = NULL` the community maps); originals stay. Temporary until the inputs are cut at source. |

## B4. models\_Monitor, algorithms, ensemble and meta-model

| Function (file) | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ALGO_MEMBERS`, `algoRegistry()` (`algoModels.R`) | Canonical member order `brt, glm, gam, rf, nn`; name to list(fit, refit, predict). A new model = one registry entry. |
| `algoFit`, `algoPredict`, `algoRefit` | Fit one family on a training table; predicted probability clipped to \[0, 1\]; refit the SAME specification on other data (CV folds, bootstrap draws) without new model selection. |
| `algoFitGLM` | Binomial GLM, linear + quadratic term per predictor, AIC `step()`, drops terms until it converges. |
| `algoFitGAM` | `mgcv::gam` binomial, `s(x, k = 4)` per predictor. Since 2026-10-08 a ladder of robust settings (REML 500 iterations, REML + efs, then k = 3) before dropping the sparsest predictor; the refit uses the same ladder. |
| `algoFitRF` | `ranger` regression forest, 1000 trees, `mtry = max(floor(p/3), 1)`, `min.node.size = 5` (matches `randomForest` defaults; documented deviation). |
| `algoFitNN` / `algoPredictNN` | `nnet`, standardised predictors, mean of 5 starts, 3 hidden units, decay 0.1, 1000 iterations (from the 2026-10-08 pilot). |
| `algoEnsembleMean(preds)`, `ensTag(members)` | Arithmetic mean over members (NA where any member is NA); the tag used in file and folder names: `ens` for brt+glm+gam+rf, else `ens_<members joined by "-">`. |
| `ensFile`, `ensPredictors`, `ensClimateFile`, `ensCovStack` (`algoScale.R`) | Paths and inputs of the ensemble files. |
| `brtMemberRun(cfg, sp, scale)` | Makes the BRT a member: rebuilds its out-of-fold predictions from the saved fold models, no refitting. |
| `algoScaleRun(cfg, sp, scale, algo, threads, years)` | One (species, scale, algorithm) job: fit, block-CV and out-of-fold predictions at the habitat records in one pass, then prediction maps for all years. Existing complete files are reused. |
| `ensembleScaleRun(cfg, sp, scale, members, years)` (`ensembleScale.R`) | Ensemble of any member set for one scale: mean out-of-fold prediction, performance table, mean map and SD across members. |
| `predictModelToRaster(...)` | Algorithm-agnostic blockwise prediction onto a raster (the BRT version `predictBRTToRaster` is separate). |
| `metaModel(...)` (`metaModel.R`) | The meta-model event. `scaleSource` = `brt` or an ensemble name; `honestCfg` = out-of-fold weights and accuracy. Remembers which ridge made the existing maps (`_meta_ridgeid.txt`) and rebuilds every year if the weights changed. |
| `fitRidgeCv(x, y, ...)` (`fitRidgeCv.R`) | The single place a ridge is fitted: `cv.glmnet`, binomial, alpha 0, `lower.limits = 0` (no negative weights). |
| `fitRidgeOneSpecies`, `evalRidgeOneSpecies`, `blockCVPredictRidge` | Ridge with 10-fold CV (seed 42, `lambda.1se`); its block-CV evaluation; nested block CV of the ridge. |
| `metaOutOfFoldCheck(cfg, sp)`, `metaOutOfFoldEnsemble(cfg, sp, tag)` | Honest meta-model inputs: each habitat record predicted by a fold model that never saw its block (habitat: own fold; climate and landscape: the fold of the nearest record). Refits the ridge on in-sample and out-of-fold inputs and compares; returns `perfOutOfFold` and the out-of-fold inputs used as ridge training data. The second is the ensemble twin. |
| `metaClimateStamp(cfg, sp)` | md5 of the climate windows of the habitat years: a saved check made from different climate files is never reused. |
| `loadSuitability(scale, spClean, year, modelDirs, refRaster)` | Reads a scale's `mean_prob` map (BRT, or the ensemble named in `birdMonitor.scaleSource`) and resamples it bilinearly onto the 200 m reference grid. |
| Other files changed since 2026-10-05 | `blockCVPredictRidge.R`, `bootstrapMetaModelTrend.R`, `computeVariableImportance.R`, `fitDevRatio.R` (non-negative ridge), `determineBlockSize.R`, `optimizeBRT.R` (now reports the real `gbm.step` error), `predictBRTToRaster.R` (blockwise reads), `modelGerHabitat.R` (year chunks), `modelEurope.R` (cache key). |

## B5. runIndex\_Monitor

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `computeAnnualReport(...)` | Builds the report: species index (100 x area mean / baseline) via `extractMetaProbSeries` and `computeSpeciesIndex`; spatial SE via `extractMetaProbSD`; four combined indices (SBI `computeCombinedIndex`, Analytical `computeCombinedIndexAnalytical`, MSI `computeCombinedIndexMSI`, Chain `computeChainIndex`, plus Chain restricted to `restrictedYears`); richness map (`computeSRMap`); change maps for the three comparisons. Does not keep change rasters in memory (killed an EVE job at 32 GB). |
| `extractMetaProbSeries(species, years, metaDir)` | Area mean of `meta_prob` per year over all non-NA pixels of the file (no boundary). Unchanged. |
| `computeChangeMaps(...)` | Per species 3 layers: `deltaP`, `gainLoss` (0 stable absent, 1 loss, 2 gain, 3 stable present), `stableIncDec` (-1/0/1). Community 5 layers: `meanDeltaP`, `netGainLoss`, `gainCount`, `lossCount`, `turnoverBC` (new 2026-10-08). |
| `computeIndexUncertainty(...)` | (1) Stitches the community pieces. (2) Reads each species' area-mean file and drops replicate 0. (3) Inside each replicate: species index, SBI (geometric mean), Chain (cumulated geometric mean of year-to-year ratios), then mean, median and percentile interval across replicates. (4) Analytical and MSI use the SD of the species index across replicates as the standard error. Only replicates common to all species enter the combined indices. |
| `computeRegionalIndexUncertainty(...)` | Step `regionindex`. Per grid size: combined index per cell, year and replicate from the stored cell means, then summaries over replicates (year maps, 3 change maps, trend per decade, shares), a coverage layer, the replicate array, and a parity check of replicate 0 against the baseline raw regional index. Helpers: `regionalCombineSpecies` (matrix version of `computeGriddedCombinedIndex`: species index = 100 x mean / baseline mean, a species left out of a cell where the baseline mean is below `minBaseline` = 1e-6; geometric mean over species), `regionalSummary`, `regionalChange`, `regionalRaster`, `regionalParity` (MISMATCH if more than 1% of cells disagree on validity or the 99th percentile of the difference exceeds 0.5 index points). |
| `computeRegionalIndex`, `computeGriddedCombinedIndex`, `aggregateSpeciesToGrid` | The baseline regional index: raw and smoothed rasters per cell size; per-cell combined index; aggregation of `meta_prob` to coarse cells (optionally masked to the country first). Unchanged. |

| --- | --- |
| `transformToLAEA(x, tolM = 2)` (`transformToLAEA.R`) | Transforms an sf object to EPSG:3035. Tries the PROJ string, EPSG:3035 and terra, accepts the first whose coordinates match the closed-form reference within 2 m; if none does, uses the reference coordinates. Logs each method's deviation. |
| `laeaCoordinates(x, what)`, `laeaLooksLikeGermany(xy)`, `laeaCRSProj4` | Extract x/y and STOP if they look swapped or lie outside Germany's box; the explicit PROJ string of EPSG:3035. |
| `analyticLAEA`, `utm32ToLonLat`, `lonLatToLAEA` (`laeaAnalytic.R`) | Independent closed-form reference coordinates (ellipsoidal Lambert azimuthal equal-area; UTM zone 32N by Krueger series). |
| `warmUpSfProj()`, `reportAxisState(label)`, `loadedGeoLibsDP()` | One throw-away `st_transform` so sf initialises GDAL/PROJ before terra; logs the axis order and the loaded geo libraries at the start of every dataPrep event. |
| `getMonthlyFile.R`, `readDailyCropped.R` (2026-10-07) | Climate daily aggregation = mean (not min/max); fill values cleaned; months with fewer than 90% of the days not used; failed remote reads retried and re-read. New cache name `_dmean`. |
| `occurrencePrep*.R`, `occurrenceCacheSchema.R`, `reportDroppedRows.R` | Occurrence tables per scale; cache schema number in the cache key; reports every dropped row and why. |

# 5. Running on the cluster, step by step

How to run the whole workflow on the UFZ cluster EVE from a login node, in order, with the commands, what to check after each step, how long it takes, and what to do when something fails. Every command block starts with `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor`.

**Conventions.**

- `<run>` is the baseline run folder, `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME` (default `test4` in every script). Use the same value in every step.
- `<tag>` is the uncertainty run tag, `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG`. The BRT-only run uses `honest2`; the big 5 run uses `ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn`.
- There are 14 species since 28 October (`sharedSpecies`, the `include = "X"` rows of `data/speciesCanonical.csv`); there were 11 for the runs in sections 7.1 to 7.11. Since 21 October the array jobs of the clean-run chain follow the roster size; older scripts (the one-off scripts of tab 4, part A6) still say `--array=1-11`.
- The uncertainty folder is `outputs/<run>/uncertainty_<tag>`; the replicate label in file names is `reps_000-050` for replicates 0 to 50.

**General rules.**

1. Log in with `ssh frontend1.eve.ufz.de` (UFZ VPN needed).
2. Use `bash --login cluster/<script>.sh` for every script that loads modules. Without a login shell the `module` command does not exist and the script prints "The 'module' command is missing" and stops.
3. Everything is under `outputs/<run>/` on `/work`, where files untouched for 60 days are deleted and there is no backup. Copy what you want to keep to `/data/birds` or a PC.
4. Update the code first: `git pull` and `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
5. While jobs run, use read-only commands only: `squeue -u $USER`, `bash cluster/status.sh <ids>`, `bash cluster/monitor_chains.sh`, `bash cluster/job_timings.sh <ids>`, `sacct`.
6. Never submit the same workflow twice: two runs write the same files at the same time (this happened on 8 October). Most submit scripts refuse while their jobs are queued; `FORCE=1` in front overrides, and should be used only after checking `squeue -u $USER`.

## Step 0. The clean run for version 1 of the Monitor (run folder `v2`)

This replaces steps 2 to 6 for the first version of the Monitor: one command chains everything (tab 4, A1, `cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh`). It needs steps 1 (setup) and the input data. It has not been submitted yet; I wrote it on 21 October and it is on hold until the project lead says go. Do it in this order, one step at a time:

1. Check what is in `/data/birds` against the inputs (read-only; takes a few minutes): `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor && git pull -q && COPY_INPUTS=1 MODE=verify bash cluster/copy_to_data_birds.sh 2>&1 | tail -60`. If the `inputs` block is not empty, or `MISSING` appears, make the copy with `sbatch cluster/eve_copy_data_birds.sbatch` and run the check again when the job has finished.
2. Check the EBBA2 file on EVE: `ebba2_data_occurrence_50km_2026-10-28.csv` must be in `inputs/response/raw/ornitho/` (md5 `58ad0369ec0cbeb7cf17d1dc1b66a0c0`, 1,913,376 bytes, 53,447 rows, 17 species). The script prints these values at the start and writes them to `outputs/v2/RUN_INFO.txt`; compare them with this line.
3. Trial that submits nothing: `DRY_RUN=1 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` runs the checks and prints the whole chain (it writes only a species-check log in `logs/`).
4. Send it: `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor && git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive && bash --login cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh`. About 5 to 6 days (see START_HERE.md for the measured times). Monitor with `bash cluster/monitor_tonight.sh` (read-only).
5. When the connector job is done: `cat /data/birds/viz/_missing.csv` must be empty, and `grep -H RESULT outputs/v2/uncertainty*/*/parity_check.txt` must say `RESULT: OK` for every species.

The script stops by itself (and says why) if the run folder `outputs/v2` exists, if the code on EVE has uncommitted changes, if a module is not at its pinned commit, if a roster species has no records at one scale, if the EBBA2 file is missing, or if there is no safety copy. If the chain breaks in the middle, rerun with `RESUME=1` and read tab 5, "What to do when a stage fails". The preparation changes the processed inputs in place, so the safety copy is not optional.

**What you need before step 0 (once per person).** An EVE account, the UFZ VPN, the ssh settings for Windows, the clone of the repository with its submodules and the setup script are written for a newcomer in `EVE_GUIDE.md`, part A (A1 to A4); do those first. For `/data/birds` you also have to be a member of the group `eve_birds` (on 13 October: `hildebrl`, `michelet`, `quintana`). Do not run `git checkout main` inside the modules before the clean run: the script stops if a module is not at the commit the main repository points to, and `git submodule update --init --recursive` puts it there. Nobody has run step 0 end to end yet: the pieces were run separately in October, the chain only as a dry run.

**Which command for which job.** Every command starts on the EVE login node, in `~/projects/birdMonitor`, after `git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive`, with `export BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=v2` (or the name of your run) typed first in the same session. The commands marked "mirrors" are copied from lines of the chain scripts and have not been run on their own; read the script header they point to before you use them. Submit one job type at a time and look at `squeue -u $USER` first, because two copies of the same step write the same files.

| I want to... | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run the whole analysis for a new run folder | `bash --login cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` (try first with `DRY_RUN=1` in front) | Step 0 above. About 5 to 6 days. A new name for a new run: `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=<name>` |
| Continue a run that broke in the middle | `RESUME=1 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` | Only what is missing is recomputed. Tab 5, "What to do when a stage fails" |
| See how the jobs are doing (read-only) | `squeue -u $USER`, `bash cluster/monitor_tonight.sh`, `bash cluster/status.sh <jobid> <jobid> ...` | `status.sh` lists FAILED, OUT\_OF\_MEMORY, TIMEOUT and CANCELLED tasks; every submit script prints the ids it submitted. `sacct -S today -X` shows today's jobs |
| Check that a finished run is sound (read-only) | `grep -H RESULT outputs/$BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME/uncertainty*/*/parity_check.txt` and `cat outputs/$BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/regional/regional_parity_*km.txt` | Every line must say `RESULT: OK` |
| Redo the species indices and the combined index (best estimate) and the regional maps from the finished maps | `BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_index.sbatch` | Mirrors line 93 of the clean-run script. About 35 minutes. Reads `metamodel_02_1_50_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany/`. Writes `annual_report_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany/` |
| Redo the combined index with its 90% intervals (the MSI with uncertainty) from the stored replicates | `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_MEMBERS=brt,glm,gam,rf,nn BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn BIRDMONITOR_UNC_BANDS=48 BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=0:25 sbatch --export=ALL,BIRDMONITOR_UNC_AREAMEAN=area_mean_replicates_germany.csv,BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany cluster/eve_unc_assembleall.sbatch` | Mirrors lines 99 and 47 of the clean-run and regional scripts. Nothing is refitted. Writes `combined_index_uncertainty.csv` and stitches the richness maps of every year. The band number 48 must match the run (the ensemble run uses 48; with 16 only a third of the richness pieces would be stitched) |
| Redo the Germany-only copies of the meta-model maps | `MASK_META_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn sbatch --export=ALL --array=1-14 cluster/eve_mask_meta.sbatch` | Mirrors line 92 of the clean-run script; 14 = number of species |
| Add or change one species or one scale | Change the three tables in `data/`, commit module first and main repository second, pull on EVE, move the affected results aside, and submit the standard chain for all species | `UPDATING_THE_RUNS.md`, sections 2 and 4, with the moves done by a script like `cluster/refresh_climate_3species_2026-10-09.sh` (use `DRY_RUN=1` first). Never set `BIRDMONITOR_SPECIES` for this |
| Copy the results to `/data/birds` | `COPY_INPUTS=0 sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_copy_data_birds.sbatch` | Adds and updates, never deletes. Check later with `MODE=verify bash cluster/copy_to_data_birds.sh` |
| Refill the folder the Monitor reads | `sbatch cluster/eve_connector.sbatch` (`BIRDMONITOR_VIZ_DRY=1 sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_connector.sbatch` only reports) | It reads the copy in `/data/birds/birdMonitor/outputs`, so copy first. Then `cat /data/birds/viz/_missing.csv` must be empty |
| Change the cut-off year of the preliminary national trend | `BIRDMONITOR_NATIONAL_LAST_YEAR=2024 sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_connector.sbatch` | Only the connector is rerun; no model job |
| Make the figures again | `FIG_ARGS="--sections S9 --variants big5" sbatch --export=ALL cluster/eve_figures.sbatch` | Sections S2 to S9; see the header of `tools/makeResultFigures.R` |

Do not use `scancel` or delete files under `outputs/` unless you know what depends on them: a cancelled job cancels everything that waits for it (`--kill-on-invalid-dep`), and results are never deleted, only moved aside to `outputs/<run>/_old_<date>/`.

## Step 1. One-time setup

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
bash --login cluster/setup_eve.sh
```

This takes 30 to 60 minutes the first time and is safe to rerun. It loads the modules, creates `/work/$USER/birdMonitor/{inputs,cache,outputs,tmp}`, links `inputs/`, `cache/` and `outputs/` to them, installs the R packages, and submits a 10-minute smoke test. About a minute later, `cat logs/smoketest_<jobid>.err` must end with `SMOKETEST: ALL OK`. Then copy the input data (about 60 GB, not in git) to `/work/$USER/birdMonitor/inputs/` (`rsync` from `/data/birds/inputs/`, or WinSCP); never into `/home`. Finally install the extra packages for the uncertainty and ensemble workflows:

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
bash --login cluster/setup_uncertainty.sh
```

The printed table must show no `MISSING` (matrixStats, ranger, nnet, mgcv, geodata, gbm, glmnet, terra, sf, blockCV). `nnet` was missing on 9 October and is now installed by this script. If it stops, run it again: it continues.

## Step 2. Baseline pipeline

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive
BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=test4 bash cluster/submit_eve_pipeline.sh
```

The chain is: prep, then the three model arrays (europe, habitat, landscape; the meta-model of a species runs inside whichever of its scale tasks finishes last), then the index (waits for prep and for every array task to end, so one failed species does not block the others). The script prints the job ids. It has no double-submission guard: check `squeue -u $USER` first.

The habitat array reads a covariate cache written by `sbatch cluster/eve_covcache.sbatch` (1 to 2 minutes per year, 4 h limit). `submit_eve_pipeline.sh` does not submit it: if `outputs/<run>/uncertainty/covcache/scale_02/` is missing (for example deleted by the 60-day rule), submit it first and wait for it to finish before the habitat array starts.

Check with `bash cluster/status.sh <prep> <europe> <habitat> <landscape> <index>`. Durations: europe array about 10 minutes; habitat 57 to 154 minutes per species locally (limit 12 h); landscape 16 to 71 minutes locally (limit 5 h); meta-model about 15 minutes for the array; index about 35 minutes (measured, peak 20 GB). Then `Rscript tools/collectPerformance.R test4` writes `outputs/test4/performance_table.csv`.

If prep fails, its dependents are cancelled; read `logs/prep_<jobid>.err`, fix, rerun the same script (finished work is reused). If one species fails in an array, the index still runs without it and names it in a warning; rerun only its meta-model with `sbatch --array=<species number> modules/models_Monitor/cluster/eve_array_meta.sbatch`. After a rerun of an array, the meta-model does NOT start by itself (found on 8 October): submit the meta array explicitly, then the index with `--dependency=afterok:<meta job>`.

## Step 3. Germany-only copies and Germany-only baseline index

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
bash --login cluster/submit_eve_germany_baseline.sh
```

It runs `mask-meta` (11 tasks) and then the index with the tag `germany`. Results: `metamodel_<res>_germany/`, `annual_report_germany/`, `regional_index_germany/`; the whole-box versions stay for comparison. The index takes about 35 minutes plus a few minutes of masking. Read-only checks: `sbatch cluster/eve_check_germany_share.sbatch` (share of pixels outside Germany) and `sbatch cluster/eve_floor_counts.sbatch` (cells near the baseline floor of the regional index).

## Step 4. BRT-only uncertainty

Prerequisite: the baseline of Step 2 has finished; the preflight lists any missing main model, training table or covariate file. A cheap test first (replicate 0 plus 3 replicates, one year, folder `uncertainty_timing`, which never mixes with real replicates):

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG=timing BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=0:3 BIRDMONITOR_UNC_YEARS=2025 UNC_THROTTLE=40 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_uncertainty.sh
```

The real run (replicate 0 plus 50 replicates, all years, 16 bands, therefore 176 band tasks):

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG=honest2 UNC_THROTTLE=100 UNC_BAND_TIME=24:00:00 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_uncertainty.sh
```

The script runs the preflight on the login node and submits covcache, prepare (11 species), band (176), summarize (176), assemble (11) and community (16), and finally assembleall, each waiting for the previous one. To queue it behind a baseline that is still running, add `UNC_AFTER=<job id>` (the preflight then runs inside the first job); never give a job id that has already finished, because the scheduler forgets finished jobs after a few minutes and refuses a dependency on them.

**Measured durations of the first BRT-only run:** prepare 0.4 h wall; band stage 176 tasks, mean 2.9 h, longest 11 h, wall 13.9 h (so the default 12 h limit is too tight: use 24 h); summarize 0.5 h; assemble 0.2 h; community 0.3 h. Replicate files total about 100 GB for all species.

**Check:** `bash cluster/status.sh <covcache> <prepare> <band> <summarize> <assemble> <community> <assembleall>` and `bash cluster/job_timings.sh <ids>`. When everything is COMPLETED, every species must say `RESULT: OK`:

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
grep -H RESULT outputs/test4/uncertainty_honest2/*/parity_check.txt
```

A `MISMATCH` means replicate 0 does not reproduce the baseline map: use the diagnostics of Step 7. **Resume after a failure:** rerun the same command with the same settings; finished work is detected and skipped. **Add replicates later:** `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=51:100` (a new run label; the old files stay). This script has no double-submission guard.

## Step 5. Regional index and Germany-only steps (BRT-only)

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
BIRDMONITOR_UNC_TAG=honest2 UNC_AFTER=<band job id of Step 4> UNC_FINAL=<assembleall job id of Step 4> UNC_THROTTLE=100 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_regional.sh
```

The chain is regionband (176 tasks), regionassemble (11), regionindex (once); in parallel after regionassemble, assembleAll again with the German-only area means (it also waits for `UNC_FINAL`, so the two never write at once) and then maskmaps (12 tasks). Tag, replicates and bands must match Step 4. If the band stage has already finished, leave out `UNC_AFTER` and `UNC_FINAL`. Durations: minutes.

Check with `bash cluster/status.sh` for the five job ids, and read the parity of the three grids:

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
cat outputs/test4/uncertainty_honest2/regional/regional_parity_*km.txt
```

Every grid must say `RESULT: OK`. Results are in `<uncertainty folder>/regional/`, `maps_germany/`, `community_germany/` and `outputs/<run>/annual_report_germany/`; `Rscript tools/summarizeIndexUncertainty.R test4` prints the intervals.

## Step 6. The algorithm ensemble ("big 5": BRT, GLM, GAM, random forest, neural network)

**6a. Baseline ensemble** (fits, ensemble means, honest meta-model, index):

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
ENS_ALGOS="glm gam rf nn" ENS_VARIANTS="brt,glm,gam,rf,nn" ENS_THROTTLE=11 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_ensemble.sh | tee big5_baseline.out
```

Prerequisites: Step 2 finished (the BRT maps are members) and `setup_uncertainty.sh` run. The output includes `meta ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn: <job id>`. The Germany-only copy and index of the big 5 are then submitted by hand (the drafted script `submit_eve_tonight.sh` contained them):

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
META=<meta job id printed above>
MK=$(MASK_META_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn sbatch --parsable --export=ALL --dependency=afterok:$META --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes cluster/eve_mask_meta.sbatch)
BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG=ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany sbatch --parsable --export=ALL --dependency=afterok:$MK --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes cluster/eve_index.sbatch
```

If `META` has already finished, drop the `--dependency` option. The fits finished within hours on 9 October; the time limits are habitat 12 h, landscape 6 h, climate 3 h per task. Check the ensemble accuracy with `grep -h 'ensemble block-CV' logs/ens-mean_*.err | cut -c1-230` and the meta-model weights (zero or positive, out-of-fold) with `grep -h -E 'Coefficients|Performance \(' logs/meta_*.err | tail -22`. A task that hits its time limit resumes when submitted again; to redo one scale and model, use for example `ENS_ALGOS="gam" ENS_SCALES="landscape"`.

**6b. Ensemble uncertainty** (the ensemble inside every bootstrap replicate). Prerequisites: the members fitted (6a), the baseline ensemble and its meta-model (for the replicate-0 parity check) and the habitat covariate cache.

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
ENS_MEMBERS=brt,glm,gam,rf,nn BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=0:25 UNC_BAND_TIME=24:00:00 UNC_PREP_TIME=24:00:00 bash --login cluster/submit_eve_ensemble_uncertainty.sh
```

It uses 48 bands (528 band tasks), a throttle of 100, and the tag `ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn`, so results are in `outputs/<run>/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/`. **6c.** `bash --login cluster/submit_eve_big5_uncertainty.sh` does 6b with 25 replicates and then Step 5 for the ensemble in one command (the Germany-only index folder is then `annual_report_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany`). Replicates 26 to 50 can be added with `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=26:50`.

**Lessons from the first big 5 run (relevant for any rerun):**

- **Memory.** The default `eve_unc_prepare.sbatch` requests 8 cpus with 8 GB each (64 GB). Three species needed more (the completed tasks peaked at 51 GB, three others exceeded 64 GB). Resubmit prepare with `--mem-per-cpu=16G` (128 GB); `resume_big5_prepare_2026-10-09.sh` shows how. The submit scripts do not set this, so a fresh big 5 run must be given the memory.
- **GAM refits.** One failing GAM refit on a bootstrap resample used to take down the whole batch of its CPU core. Refits now try robust settings first; if one still fails, the main fit stands in and the case is logged in `<species>/models/refit_fallbacks.csv`. Check it after the run and report how often a fallback occurred.
- **Time.** The band tasks are one third of the area but 4 to 5 times slower than in the BRT-only run: use a 24 h limit. The band stage of 528 tasks is the long part (about 30 hours estimated).
- **Penalty rule.** Replicate ridge penalties use the baseline's rule (ten random folds) since 10 October; the earlier block-fold results are kept as a sensitivity analysis.
- **Parity.** After the run: `grep -H RESULT outputs/test4/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/*/parity_check.txt` and `cat outputs/test4/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/regional/regional_parity_*km.txt`.

## Step 7. Parity checks and diagnostics (read-only)

Replicate 0 must reproduce the baseline. Per species: `grep -H RESULT outputs/<run>/uncertainty*/*/parity_check.txt` (all `RESULT: OK`). Regional: `cat outputs/<run>/uncertainty_<tag>/regional/regional_parity_*km.txt`. Ridge weights: `BIRDMONITOR_RUNNAME=<run> Rscript tools/checkRidgeParity.R <tag>` (`maxDiff` about 0).

If a species shows MISMATCH, in this order (as on 9 October; the wrappers hard-code tag `honest2` and label `reps_000-050`, so call the R tools directly with arguments for other runs):

1. `sbatch cluster/eve_diag_parity.sbatch` (ridge weights, penalty, out-of-fold inputs), or `Rscript tools/diagnoseParity.R <run> <tag> <label>`.
2. `sbatch cluster/eve_diag_parity_maps.sbatch` (scale maps at random German pixels).
3. `sbatch cluster/eve_diag_parity_models.sbatch` (same number of trees in the baseline BRT and the replicate-0 copy?). The cause on 9 October: a refit of the baseline climate BRT after the replicate copy was made. **Rule: after refitting baseline models, re-copy or rerun replicate 0.**

Other read-only diagnostics: `Rscript tools/diagnoseReplicateBias.R <run> <tag> <label> 2025` (replicates vs baseline trend), `Rscript tools/diagnoseYearJump.R "<species list>" --tag <tag>` (last-year jumps), `Rscript tools/diagnoseBRT.R "<Genus species>" climate` (why a BRT fails), `sbatch cluster/eve_meta_check.sbatch` then `Rscript tools/runMetaCheck.R --collect` (honest accuracy of the combined map), `Rscript tools/collectPerformance.R <run>`, `Rscript tools/checkClimateWindows.R`, `Rscript tools/checkClimateMonthly.R`. The wrappers write `logs/diag_*_<jobid>.out`; read them with `cat`. Use compute nodes (sbatch), not the login node, for anything that touches rasters.

## Step 8. Monitoring

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor
squeue -u $USER -o "%.14i %.16j %.8T %.10M %R"      # what runs or waits; why waiting: squeue -t pd -o "%i %R"
bash cluster/status.sh <jobid> [<jobid> ...]           # tasks per state + problems + queue
bash cluster/job_timings.sh <jobid> [...]              # min/mean/max task hours and wall
bash cluster/monitor_chains.sh                         # the 8-12 Oct chains, then the newest chain found by itself
sacct -j <jobid> -X -n --format=JobID%16,JobName%16,State%14,Elapsed,ExitCode,MaxRSS,ReqMem
quota-eve                                              # disk quota
```

States: COMPLETED, RUNNING, PENDING; FAILED, OUT\_OF\_MEMORY, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED and NODE\_FAIL need a look. `scancel --me` cancels everything; to cancel one chain use `scancel <ids>`.

## What to do when a stage fails

1. **Find the failed task:** `bash cluster/status.sh <ids>`, or `sacct -j <jobid> -X -n --format=JobID%16,JobName%16,State%14,Elapsed,ExitCode`.
2. **Open its log.** Array tasks: `logs/<jobname>_<jobid>_<task>.err` and `.out` (for example `unc-band_<jobid>_<task>.err`, `unc-prepare_...`, `ens-algo_...`, `mask-meta_...`, `habitat_...`). Single jobs: `index_<jobid>.err`, `covcache_<jobid>.err`, and so on. `submit_eve_ensemble.sh` renames jobs (`ens-<scale>-<algo>`) but the log files keep the names of the `#SBATCH --output` line (`ens-algo_...`).
3. **Find the real error line.** The `.err` file holds the R messages; the stop message is near the end (`tail -n 40 logs/<file>.err`). The header lines `=== uncertainty task: step = ... ===`, `species: ... | band k of n` and `=== done: <step> in N min ===` tell which step and species or band the log belongs to.
4. **Classify by State:**
   - `OUT_OF_MEMORY`: `sacct ... MaxRSS,ReqMem` shows the peak. Resubmit the failed tasks only, with more `--mem-per-cpu`. A request above about 16G per cpu is routed to the small `highmem` partition and can wait for hours.
   - `TIMEOUT`: wall limit too short. Resubmit with a larger `--time` (`UNC_BAND_TIME`, `UNC_PREP_TIME`). Ensemble fit tasks and, since 12 October, the out-of-fold step resume where they stopped.
   - `FAILED` with exit code 139 and the note "exited with code 139 AFTER finishing its work" in the log: not a failure, `unc_run` counted it as success. A `FAILED` job without that note is a real error.
   - `CANCELLED` (dependency): a predecessor failed (`--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes`). Fix the predecessor and resubmit the chain with the same script and settings.
5. **Resubmit.** Finished work is skipped: `submit_eve_uncertainty.sh` detects finished files; `eve_ens_algo.sbatch` keeps finished years; `Cache()` resumes the baseline prep. Make sure nothing of the same chain is still queued (`squeue -u $USER`); the guards stop you, but `FORCE=1` overrides them, and on 8 October a second submission made two runs write the same files.
6. **To redo only part of a chain,** use the one-off scripts as templates: they show how to move results aside (never delete), how to reuse a running prepare job (`UNC_PREPARE_JOB=<id>`), how to depend on a prepare job for only some species (`cluster/resume_big5_2026-10-12.sh` splits the band array so that ten species do not wait for the slow one), and how to re-point a held job (`scontrol update JobId=<id> Dependency=afterok:<new>` then `scontrol release <id>`).
7. **If the cause is unclear:** send the log path, the job id and the `sacct` output to the cluster admins (`wkdv-cluster@ufz.de`) or to Tati.

## Safeguards

| Safeguard | Where | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Double-submission guard (`squeue` name match, stops unless `FORCE=1`) | `submit_eve_germany_baseline.sh`, `submit_eve_regional.sh`, `submit_eve_tonight.sh`, `submit_eve_big5_uncertainty.sh`, `resume_big5_prepare_2026-10-09.sh`, `refresh_*.sh`, `resume_big5_2026-10-12.sh` (marker file) | A second submission writes the same files at the same time (happened 8 October). |
| No guard | `submit_eve_pipeline.sh`, `submit_eve_uncertainty.sh`, `submit_eve_ensemble.sh`, `submit_eve_ensemble_uncertainty.sh`, `resume_big5_2026-10-08.sh`, `resubmit_big5_downstream.sh`, `ridge_rule_big5_2026-10-10.sh` | Check `squeue -u $USER` by hand first. |
| `bash --login` | scripts that call `module load` | Without it the `module` command does not exist and the script says so and exits. |
| `cd ~/projects/birdMonitor` first | all | Submit scripts change to the repo root themselves; direct `sbatch` and the monitor commands rely on you being there. |
| `--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes`, `--dependency=afterok` | all chains | A failed step cancels what waits for it; nothing stays stuck. |
| `DRY_RUN=1` | `refresh_*.sh` | Only lists what would be moved aside. |
| Never delete | one-off scripts | Old results go to `_old_*` folders. |
| Exit-time crash handling | `unc_run` in `eve_unc_common.sh` | A done-marker written as the last act; a crash at R shutdown after complete work counts as success. |
| Preflight | `runUncertaintyTask.R --step preflight` | File-existence check of every input; on the login node, or inside the covcache job when `UNC_AFTER` is set. |
| `/work` housekeeping | EVE | Files untouched for 60 days are deleted and there is no backup; TMPDIR is a RAM disk, so jobs use `/work/$USER/birdMonitor/tmp/<jobid>` and clean up. Copy final results to `/data/birds` (planned only after results are final) or to a PC. |

**P1.1 Crop all inputs to the German study-area outline at the source.**

- *Why.* The prediction window is the bounding box of Germany: 13.9 M pixels of 200 m, 8.97 M of them inside Germany (job 63182183). Seven species were predicted over the whole window (35.4% of it outside Germany); four only inside, because their models use German-only layers. The project lead's explicit priority is that nothing is computed or predicted outside Germany: we are supposed to predict only for Germany. The bounding box comes from Lisa's code, which used a box instead of a German shapefile, and it stayed (`improvements.md`, item 19).
- *Exists now (interim).* Germany-only copies of the meta-model maps (`tools/maskMetaModels.R`), the index on them (`BIRDMONITOR_INDEX_TAG=germany`), `area_mean_replicates_germany.csv`, and `maskmaps` copies of the finished maps.
- *To do.* (1) Design a `studyArea` parameter (boundary file or GADM country, level, region; `improvements.md` item 6) instead of a hard-coded Germany. (2) Decide the scope for the climate scale, which is trained on EBBA2 50 km data for Europe: cropping its predictions is mechanical, cropping its training data is a modelling change; ask the project lead. (3) Cut the covariate preparation in `dataPrep_Monitor` (climate, elevation, land use, land cover, derived layers) to the outline and check that `inputs_Monitor`, the band prediction and `runIndex_Monitor` carry no bounding-box assumption. (4) Build the outline with the closed-form `uncOutlineLAEA()`; two places still project it with terra and carry the axis-order risk: `metaModel()` and `aggregateSpeciesToGrid()`. (5) Recompute baseline, ensemble baseline and uncertainty; sanity test: the new national means must equal the interim Germany-only means to rounding error.
- *Effort and dependencies.* 3-5 days of coding; the recompute is dominated by the uncertainty band stage. Settle P1.2 and P1.3 first so everything is recomputed once.
- *Update 29 October.* Points (1) and (3) exist since 21 October: `sharedStudyArea` (country, region or shapefile), layers cropped and masked when made, record filters for every response, the regional index boundary taken from the study area, and a hard NA check. The maps still need the `_germany` copies, because the working area is the reporting area plus a buffer (decision: the suffix stays; revisit it when a second area is run). The climate scale is still trained on all of Europe (the training window is not cropped) and predicted on the area plus one 50 km cell. Not tested end to end for any area other than Germany (a Saxony test covered the preparation stage only). Still open: crop at download time (the download still fetches more than needed), an explicit climate fit-area setting, and a water mask for the maps (version 2 of the Monitor).

**P1.2 Document the meta-model regularisation rule (decided 13 October: the baseline's rule everywhere).**

- *Why.* The size of the trends depends on how the ridge penalty is chosen. The baseline uses ten random folds. Until 10 October the replicates used spatial block folds, which gave penalties 2-3 times larger and weaker trends (combined index 2025 about 97.5 against 95.6 for the baseline, which fell outside its own interval; Perdix replicates had a penalty of 38.7 and all weights zero). The replicates now use the baseline's rule (commit e0f5fa8); block folds remain available as `BIRDMONITOR_UNC_RIDGEFOLDS=block`. The caveat: random folds can under-regularise because of spatial autocorrelation.
- *Decided.* Main model and replicates use ten random folds; the block-fold results are kept as a sensitivity analysis and are not a point for the Steering Consortium (the project lead discusses modelling choices with individual modellers of the Consortium). Perdix perdix: 9 of 50 replicates have a constant map; see `improvements.md` item 17 and section 7.4.
- *To do.* Compare the two rules on the stored replicates (`_old_ridge_blockfolds_2026-10-10/` holds the old interval tables); decide the headline rule for baseline and replicates together; report the other as a sensitivity analysis; write the decision and the caveat into `DECISIONS.md` and the methods. If the headline rule becomes block folds, the baseline `metaModel()` and all replicates change together.
- *Effort.* 1-2 days if the stored replicates suffice. Decide before the P1.1 recompute.

**P1.3 Keep replicate 0 and the baseline climate models consistent.**

- *Why.* The europe array refits the climate BRTs whenever it runs, and `gbm.step` is stochastic, so the tree count can change (on 8 October: Anthus 1750 against 2400, Vanellus 2400 against 2300, Sturnus 1300 against 1350). Replicate 0 held the older copy and the parity check failed for two species. The refresh of 9 October fixed it: all 11 species and the three regional grids now pass parity.
- *To do.* Make it permanent: seed the climate `gbm.step` fit (compare `modelEurope` with `modelGerLandscape.R`, which already seeds via `stableSeed`) or add a guard that refuses a replicate-0 copy older than the baseline model (related guards exist: `metaClimateStamp`). Re-run the parity check after every baseline refit, including the big 5.
- *Effort.* 0.5-1 day. Complete before the P1.1 recompute.

**P1.4 Bring the big 5 uncertainty from 25 to 50 replicates.**

- *Why.* The big 5 was run with replicates 0:25 against 50 for the BRT-only run; with 25 the 5th and 95th percentiles each rest on one or two replicates.
- *To do.* Add replicates 26:50 (`BIRDMONITOR_UNC_REPS=26:50` in `cluster/submit_eve_big5_uncertainty.sh`), rebuild summaries, regional steps and Germany-only copies, and report how often the GAM refit fell back to the main fit (`<species>/models/refit_fallbacks.csv`).
- *Effort.* About 30 h of cluster time for the band stage (estimate), half a day of work. Do it once, after P1.1 and P1.2.

**P1.5 State the hindcast limit and validate it where possible.**

- *Why.* The habitat model is trained on 2022-2025 only and applied to 2005-2021 layers; the intervals do not include the assumption that habitat preferences were the same earlier.
- *To do.* Put the limitation into the methods, the output guide and every caption for 2005-2021 maps and trends; look for independent historical data (for example DDA territory data before 2022) as a check; run the temporal hold-out of `improvements.md` item 10 (refit the habitat BRT on 2022-2024, validate on 2025), described honestly as a one-year-forward test; add literature precedents for asymmetric training windows.
- *Effort.* Writing 0.5 day; hold-out 2-3 days; historical validation depends on the data.

**P1.6 Archive inputs, baseline and final runs to `/data/birds` (time-critical).**

- *Why.* `/work` deletes files not accessed for 60 days, so the master copy of the inputs is at risk from about 15 November 2026. `/data/birds` has a 4 TB block quota (hard limit 5 TB), a 5 million file quota, no backup and no deletion.
- *To do.* Copy final outputs only when results are settled (the project lead's decision of 7 October, repeated on 13 October: wait until the big 5 run is finished). Access is in place: `/data/birds` is owned by `michelet`, group `eve_birds` (`hildebrl`, `michelet`, `quintana`), group read and write; read `quota.txt` there for the real quota; if they are not settled by about 1 November, make a safety copy of the inputs anyway. Measure sizes first; use plain `rsync` with a checksum manifest; count files, because many small raster pieces per replicate may matter.
- *Effort.* 0.5 day plus transfer time.
- *Update 29 October.* `cluster/copy_to_data_birds.sh` and `cluster/eve_copy_data_birds.sbatch` do the copy (rsync, adds and updates only; `MODE=verify` is the read-only check); the clean-run script refuses to start without a safety copy of the processed inputs. I did not check on 29 October what is in `/data/birds`. What the copy leaves out by default (per-replicate predictions, band pieces, the covariate cache, the content-based `cache/`) is listed in tab 1, "What lives where".

**P1.7 Correct stale statements in the documentation.**

- *Why.* `UNCERTAINTY.md` still says the scale models are evaluated in-sample at the meta-model step (weights have been out-of-fold since 6 October) and that the algorithm ensemble is planned (it is built); `DECISIONS.md` lists per-species `resolution_m` as without consuming code although it was implemented on 28 September.
- *To do.* Read these against the code and fix or date-stamp each statement.
- *Effort.* 0.5-1 day.

# 7. Diagnostics, logs and results details

This section collects what the methods document deliberately leaves out: fixes, checks and logged information, so that nothing exists only in a log file. Where a number is not available yet, the cell says so and the command that produces it is given.

## 7.1 Germany-only numbers

All national and regional numbers describe Germany only; the first versions of 8 October did not.

**What was wrong.** The prediction window is the bounding box of Germany: 13.9 million pixels of 200 m, of which 8.97 million lie inside Germany. Seven species were predicted over the whole box, so 35.4% of their pixels lay in neighbouring countries and the sea. The other four species (Emberiza citrinella, Lanius collurio, Lullula arborea, Sturnus vulgaris) were predicted only inside Germany, because their models use two layers that exist only for Germany (hedges and landscape heterogeneity; this follows from the predictor lists, the layers themselves were not opened). The national indices therefore averaged different areas for different species.

**What we did.** Germany-only copies of every meta-model map were made with the German outline (GADM level 0, applied with a closed-form coordinate transformation, because the standard projection of the European grid can swap its axes on the cluster). The baseline index, the regional index and the combined indices were recomputed on them, and the replicate area means are recomputed from German pixels only. The uncertainty maps are copied the same way. The original rectangle results are kept for comparison.

| Species | Index 2025, whole box | Index 2025, Germany only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Saxicola rubetra | 88.1 | 82.7 |
| Vanellus vanellus | 95.1 | 90.8 |
| Perdix perdix | 93.3 | 91.1 |
| Alauda arvensis | 96.7 | 94.9 |
| Anthus pratensis | 97.0 | 95.7 |
| Buteo buteo | 98.5 | 97.7 |
| Emberiza calandra | 102.7 | 102.6 |
| Lanius collurio, Lullula arborea, Emberiza citrinella, Sturnus vulgaris (within 0.1 in both versions) | unchanged | unchanged |
| **Combined index (SBI)** | **97.1** | **95.6** |

**Planned.** After the Steering Consortium meeting, every input will be cut to the study-area outline at the source, so that nothing is computed or predicted outside Germany. The Germany-only copies are the interim fix and give the same numbers inside Germany.

## 7.2 Replicate 0 against the baseline (parity check)

Replicate 0 is the main model run through the machinery of the bootstrap. It must reproduce the baseline maps and indices (same valid pixels, probabilities equal within the storage precision of 3.3 x 10^-5, area means equal to about 10^-10), otherwise the intervals would be centred on something other than the main result. The check is written to `parity_check.txt` in each species folder and, for the regional index, to `regional/regional_parity_<km>km.txt`.

| Date | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9 October | BRT-only | Nine of the 11 species and all three regional grids passed. Anthus pratensis and Sturnus vulgaris differed slightly: by at most 0.003 in probability, and by 0.3% (Anthus) and 0.02% (Sturnus) in the national mean, above the strict tolerance of 0.001 for single pixels. |
| 9 October | BRT-only | Cause found: after the climate-data correction the climate-scale model of three species (Anthus pratensis, Vanellus vanellus, Sturnus vulgaris) was refitted on 8 October and ended with a slightly different number of trees, because the internal cross-validation that chooses it is random, while the replicates kept the settings of the earlier fit. Vanellus was not visibly affected because its climate weight is close to zero. The three species were refreshed the same day. |
| 13 October | BRT-only, after the change of the penalty rule | All 11 species and all three grids pass (`RESULT: OK`). |
| 13 October | big 5 | All 11 species and all three regional grids pass (`RESULT: OK`), checked with `grep -H RESULT outputs/test4/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/*/parity_check.txt` and `cat outputs/test4/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/regional/regional_parity_*km.txt`. |

Rule learned: after refitting baseline models, copy or rerun replicate 0 again.

## 7.3 Refits that failed in the big 5 bootstrap (`refit_fallbacks.csv`)

If a member (in practice the GAM) cannot be refitted on a resample even with its most robust settings, the main fit of that member stands in for that replicate, and the case is written to `outputs/test4/uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/<Species>/models/refit_fallbacks.csv` with the columns `species`, `scale`, `member`, `runLabel`, `replicate` and `reason`. The same information appears in the job log (`logs/unc-prepare_<jobid>_<task>.err`) as "N of M replicate refits FAILED".

**Result (13 October).** No `refit_fallbacks.csv` exists in any species folder of the big 5 run, so no refit needed the main fit to stand in. The file is only created when a refit fails, so its absence means zero cases. The three species that finished before the robust refit was introduced (tasks 3, 7 and 11 of the first run) also ended without a failure. To double-check against the job logs, this command should print nothing:

```bash
cd ~/projects/birdMonitor && grep -l "replicate refits FAILED" logs/unc-prepare_63480553_*.err logs/unc-prepare_63257254_*.err
```

| Species | Scale | Member | Replicates where the main fit stood in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all 11 species | all three scales | GLM, GAM, random forest, neural network | 0 (no file written) |

## 7.4 Replicates with a constant map (Perdix perdix)

In the BRT-only run, 9 of the 50 replicates of Perdix perdix have an index of exactly 100 in every year (replicates 5, 11, 16, 18, 21, 29, 33, 37 and 42), so the map of such a replicate is constant: the meta-model found no usable signal in that resample. Perdix has the largest ridge penalty of all species also in the main model (0.264, against 0.04 to 0.15). It is not yet confirmed that this is the only species, and that all weights are zero in those replicates. The replicates stay in the interval for now (a bootstrap repeats the main procedure); the second interval without them is item 17 of `improvements.md`, to be done after the Steering Consortium meeting, with the script `tools/sensitivityConstantReplicates.R`.

## 7.5 Accuracy and weights of the big 5

These numbers belong here and not in the methods document. They come from the big 5 baseline run (finished 9 October); the sources are `logs/ens-mean_*.err` (accuracy of the ensembles and of their members) and `logs/meta_*.err` (meta-model).

**Accuracy of the ensembles.** Block-cross-validated AUC of the average of the five algorithms at each scale; in brackets the AUC of the BRT alone at the same scale. The ensemble is better than the BRT in 31 of 33 species-scale combinations (mean gain 0.019: 0.017 at the climate scale, 0.028 at the landscape scale and 0.012 at the habitat scale; largest gain 0.039). The two exceptions are Vanellus vanellus at the climate scale (0.845 against 0.847) and Emberiza calandra at the habitat scale (0.943 against 0.948). AUCs of different scales are not comparable, because each scale is tested on different records.

## 7.7 Reproducing a run

The code is in the repository `tati-micheletti/birdMonitor` (four modules). On the cluster, the workflow is a chain of dependent jobs started by the scripts in `cluster/`: the baseline (`submit_eve_pipeline.sh`), the Germany-only baseline (`submit_eve_germany_baseline.sh`), the BRT-only uncertainty (`submit_eve_uncertainty.sh`), the regional and Germany-only uncertainty steps (`submit_eve_regional.sh`) and the big 5 (`submit_eve_ensemble.sh` and `submit_eve_ensemble_uncertainty.sh`). Every script prints the job numbers it submits and a read-only command to check progress, and refuses to run twice while its jobs are queued. The step-by-step guide is section 5. Since 21 October there is one script that chains all of these for a new run folder, `cluster/submit_eve_clean_run.sh` (section 5, step 0).


## 7.8 Results: BRT only and big 5 side by side

All numbers are Germany only, index 2025 with 2005 = 100, 90% intervals. BRT-only: main model, interval from 50 replicates. Big 5: main model, interval from 25 replicates, whose 5th and 95th percentiles are noisy. The replicate means of the combined index are 96.1 (BRT only, median 96.3) and 93.5 (big 5).

| Species | BRT only: main model | BRT only: 90% interval | Big 5: main model | Big 5: 90% interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Saxicola rubetra | 82.7 | 75.2 to 92.7 | 77.1 | 70.0 to 88.5 |
| Vanellus vanellus | 90.8 | 90.2 to 95.6 | 92.6 | 90.2 to 95.5 |
| Perdix perdix | 91.1 | 84.7 to 100.0 | 84.1 | 77.4 to 98.3 |
| Alauda arvensis | 94.9 | 93.7 to 95.8 | 94.3 | 93.3 to 95.0 |
| Anthus pratensis | 95.7 | 84.6 to 97.2 | 92.1 | 86.0 to 94.3 |
| Lanius collurio | 97.3 | 96.0 to 99.5 | 95.5 | 89.8 to 97.7 |
| Emberiza citrinella | 97.4 | 96.7 to 98.0 | 97.6 | 96.6 to 97.8 |
| Buteo buteo | 97.7 | 97.5 to 98.7 | 97.8 | 97.3 to 98.3 |
| Sturnus vulgaris | 98.8 | 98.3 to 99.2 | 98.9 | 98.7 to 99.2 |
| Emberiza calandra | 102.6 | 97.2 to 118.8 | 96.8 | 91.7 to 97.8 |
| Lullula arborea | 104.5 | 98.7 to 109.8 | 102.2 | 93.4 to 106.0 |
| **Combined index (SBI)** | **95.6** | **94.0 to 98.2** | **93.3** | **91.5 to 95.7** |

The MSI gives practically the same combined index as the SBI in both runs (big 5: 93.6, 91.4 to 95.8).

What stands out:

- The big 5 shows a stronger decline than the BRT-only run: 93.3 against 95.6 for the main models (replicate means 93.5 and 96.1). The two intervals overlap only between 94.0 and 95.7.
- The largest differences between the two runs are Emberiza calandra (102.6 in the BRT-only run, a slight increase; 96.8 with the big 5, a decline whose interval 91.7 to 97.8 does not contain 100), Perdix perdix (91.1 against 84.1) and Lanius collurio (97.3 against 95.5).
- The upper end of the Perdix interval is 100 in the BRT-only run (replicates with a constant map, section 7.4) and 98.3 with the big 5. Whether the big 5 has constant replicates is not known; the check of `improvements.md` item 17 should be run for it too.
- Three species have no change between the runs beyond rounding: Emberiza citrinella, Buteo buteo and Sturnus vulgaris.


## 7.9 Which files feed which output of the monitor

This is the map from the outputs listed in decision 4 of the Steering Consortium document to the files that someone has to take from the cluster and prepare. All paths are under `outputs/test4/` (after the copy also under `/data/birds/birdMonitor/outputs/test4/`). Species file names use underscores (`Alauda_arvensis`). The BRT-only run uses the folders without a suffix and `uncertainty_honest2`; the big 5 uses the same names with the suffix `ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn` (for example `uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn`). `<comp>` is `vsBaseline` (2025 against 2005), `vs5YearsAgo` (2025 against 2020) or `vsLastYear` (2025 against 2024); `<km>` is 10, 20 or 50. The file names come from the output map in section 3 of this document; before preparing material, look at one folder to confirm them, for example `ls outputs/test4/uncertainty_honest2/Alauda_arvensis/maps_germany/`.

| Output of the monitor | Files (Germany only) | What is inside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yearly probability map per species | `metamodel_02_1_50_germany/<Species>_meta_suitability_<year>.tif` (big 5: `metamodel_02_1_50_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany/`) | Band `meta_prob` = probability of occurrence, band `binary` = presence-absence map. One file per year, 2005 to 2025 |
| Uncertainty layers of the probability map | `uncertainty_honest2/<Species>/maps_germany/<Species>_unc_<year>.tif` (big 5: `uncertainty_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn/...`) | Five layers: mean, sd, lwr (5th percentile), upr (95th percentile), width |
| Change maps with shares of replicates | `.../<Species>/maps_germany/<Species>_unc_change_<comp>.tif` | Seven layers: deltaMean, deltaSd, deltaLwr, deltaUpr, deltaWidth, shareDecrease, shareIncrease |
| Per-pixel trend per decade | `.../<Species>/maps_germany/<Species>_unc_trend_per_decade.tif` | Seven layers: slopeMean, slopeSd, slopeLwr, slopeUpr, slopeWidth, shareDecrease, shareIncrease |
| Gain and loss maps (no uncertainty) | `annual_report_germany/change_<comp>_<Species>.tif` (big 5: `annual_report_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_germany/`) | Three layers: deltaP, gainLoss (0 stable absent, 1 loss, 2 gain, 3 stable present), stableIncDec |
| Species index for Germany | `annual_report_germany/species_index.csv` (best estimate), `species_index_uncertainty.csv` (interval per species and year) | Index with 2005 = 100; columns indexMean, indexMedian, indexLwr, indexUpr |
| Combined index | `annual_report_germany/combined_index_sbi.csv`, `combined_index_msi.csv`, `combined_index_chain.csv` (best estimates), `combined_index_uncertainty.csv` (intervals; the rows "Analytical" are not reported), `uncertainty_honest2/combined_index_replicates.csv` (every replicate) | The Analytical index is dropped from all reports |
| Regional index maps | Best estimate: `regional_index_germany/regional_index_<km>km_raw.tif` and `..._smoothed.tif`. With uncertainty: `uncertainty_honest2/regional/regional_index_<km>km_unc_<year>.tif` (5 layers), `..._unc_change_<comp>.tif` and `..._unc_trend_per_decade.tif` (7 layers), `..._coverage.tif` (share of each cell inside Germany) | The smoothed map has no interval |
| Expected richness | `uncertainty_honest2/community_germany/richness_expected_unc_<year>.tif`; best estimate: `annual_report_germany/SR_map_2025.tif` | Sum of the probabilities over species. The `test4` runs have the uncertainty file for 2025 only; the clean run `v2` writes every year (since 28 October). The best estimate `SR_map_<year>.tif` is still for the report year only |
| National trend (clean run only) | `annual_report_<tag>_germany/combined_index_uncertainty.csv`, which the connector turns into `/data/birds/viz/msi_national/msi_national.csv` | Method, year, estimate, median, lwr, upr, and the `preliminary` flag for the years after the last published national indicator year |
| Mean change and turnover | `uncertainty_honest2/community_germany/community_meanDeltaP_unc_<comp>.tif` (7 layers) and `community_turnoverBC_unc_<comp>.tif` (5 layers); best estimates: `annual_report_germany/change_<comp>_community.tif` (5 layers: meanDeltaP, netGainLoss, gainCount, lossCount, turnoverBC) | Turnover is Bray-Curtis |
| Model accuracy per species and scale | Tables in section 7.5 of this document; `performance_table.csv` (made by `Rscript tools/collectPerformance.R test4`); per species `<Species>_perf_meta.rds` in the meta-model folder | Honest AUC; weights of the three scales |
| Spread among the five algorithms (big 5 only) | `scale_50/`, `scale_1/` and `scale_02/` (climate, landscape, habitat): `<Species>_sd_ens_brt-glm-gam-rf-nn_<scale>_<year>.tif` | Standard deviation across the five algorithms |
| BRT only against big 5 | The two sets of folders above, side by side; section 7.8 for the numbers | Shows what the ensemble adds |

The maps are large, so Lisa should copy only what a figure needs. The indices are small tables (CSV) and can be taken in full. Two more things she needs: the species list and their names (`data/speciesCanonical.csv` in the repository) and the German outline (`inputs/predictors/raw/gadm/`) for the map frames.

## 7.10 Problems found between 5 and 13 October and how they were fixed

This is the list that used to be the appendix of the executive summary.

Twelve problems turned up between 5 and 13 October. Three changed the results (the climate data, the neighbouring countries, and how the bootstrap replicates weight the scales) and all three are corrected. One left a small difference in two species that is understood and was then removed. One (the grey partridge) is stated as a caveat and gets a second interval after the meeting. The others only cost time.

| # | Problem (when found) | Cause | Fix | Effect on results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Unexplained drops of several species indices in 2025 (7 Oct) | From 2022 the daily climate files were summarised as the minimum of daily minima and the maximum of daily maxima instead of means, unlike the monthly files used before; remote downloads that failed in part returned zeros or fill values (for example 6,553.4 K) | Means used throughout, fill values removed, months with fewer than 90% of days skipped, failed reads repeated; four climate windows rebuilt from about 3,000 daily files; predictions, meta-models, indices and the uncertainty chain recomputed | Climate now has a positive weight for 10 of 11 species (close to zero for one), where before it was zero for 7; the 2025 drops were not caused by climate |
| 2 | National indices averaged parts of neighbouring countries (8 Oct) | The prediction window is the bounding box of Germany, 35% of which is abroad; seven species were predicted over all of it, four only inside Germany because their models use two German-only layers | Germany-only copies of all maps; baseline, regional and combined indices recomputed; replicate means recomputed for Germany only | Combined index in 2025: 95.6 instead of 97.1; seven species show 1-5 index points more decline; four species unchanged |
| 3 | Coordinates swapped in some cluster sessions (5 and 8 October) | In some R sessions on the cluster the axis order of the European projection (EPSG:3035) comes out reversed, depending on which geographic library starts first | A closed-form coordinate formula that cannot flip; checks that stop with a clear message instead of using wrong coordinates | None: prevented wrong masks and crashes |
| 4 | Overlapping jobs (8 Oct) | Two copies of the same job ran at once, and a new chain started while the file it read was being rewritten | Submission scripts refuse to run twice while their jobs are queued; dependencies between steps; the affected step was rerun | None: the affected step was rerun and checked |
| 5 | A model fit stopped (8 Oct) | The GAM for one species did not converge at the climate scale | GAM now tries more robust settings before giving up; fits that converged first time are unchanged | None |
| 6 | Neural network not converging (8 Oct) | The first settings (10 hidden units, 300 iterations) failed to converge in every landscape fit | Pilot of nine settings at three scales; chose 3 units, decay 0.1, up to 1000 iterations | The network now converges and is cheaper |
| 7 | Job chain broke on a forgotten job; a package was missing (8 Oct) | The scheduler forgets finished jobs after minutes; one R package was not installed | Dependencies only on known jobs; package installed; a package check before submission | None: delays only |
| 8 | Replicate 0 of two species differed slightly from the baseline (9 Oct) | After the climate-data correction the climate model of three species was refitted on 8 October and chose a slightly different number of trees (the internal cross-validation is random), while the bootstrap replicates kept the setting of the earlier fit | Cause identified by comparing weights, inputs, maps and models; those species were refreshed on 9 October and all 11 now pass the check | At most 0.3% of the national mean for two species; the intervals are not affected materially |
| 9 | The big 5 preparation failed for 8 of 11 species (9 Oct) | Five species: the additive-model (GAM) refit on a resampled dataset stopped with an error and took its batch of replicates with it; three species: memory above the 64 GB requested | The refit now tries more robust settings first and, if one replicate still fails, the main fit stands in and the case is logged; memory raised to 128 GB; the failed species were rerun | None on the numbers; about half a day of delay |
| 10 | Replicates showed weaker trends than the main model (9 and 10 Oct) | The replicates chose the strength of the penalty that weights the three scales with spatial-block folds, the main model with random folds; the penalty came out 2 to 3 times larger and the weights shrank | Replicates now repeat exactly the main model's procedure; the block-fold version is kept as a sensitivity analysis; the 50 replicates were recomputed on 12 and 13 October | The main-model index (95.6) lay outside the interval of its replicates (96.1 to 99.0) and now lies inside it (94.0 to 98.2); intervals computed before 10 October are replaced |
| 11 | A big 5 preparation task ran out of time (10 Oct) | One step of one species (Emberiza calandra) needed more than the 24 hours allowed and saved its result only at the very end | The step now saves after each scale; the task was resubmitted with 48 hours and the other ten species continued without waiting for it | None on the numbers; the big 5 intervals are delayed by about three days |
| 12 | Replicates of the grey partridge with a constant map (13 Oct) | In 9 of 50 resamples the meta-model of this rare species with a weak model found no usable signal, so the replicate map does not change over time | Kept, because a bootstrap repeats the main procedure; stated as a caveat in the methods | The upper end of the Perdix interval is 100; the effect on the combined index is small; a second interval without these replicates follows after the meeting |

## 7.11 Final checks of every reported number (13 October)

Done in three steps; none shows a difference.

1. **From the maps to the intervals** (`tools/checkReportedNumbers.R`, run for both runs with all 11 species for 2025, and for two species and three years in a first run): the mean of `meta_prob` of the Germany-only map, recomputed with terra, equals the area mean of replicate 0; the species index recomputed from the area means equals `species_index.csv`; the geometric mean of the 11 species indices equals the combined index of the annual report (BRT-only 95.575, big 5 93.276); and the mean and the 5th and 95th percentile of the combined index over the replicates equal `combined_index_uncertainty.csv` (BRT-only 96.147, 94.041 to 98.174; big 5 93.529, 91.546 to 95.746). 52 comparisons, 0 differences (plus 18 in the first run).
2. **From the files to the documents.** The species and combined-index tables of the executive summary and of section 7.8, and the AUC and weight tables of section 7.5, were compared with the printed result files and logs: 12 + 33 + 11 rows, no difference. The main-model values of the BRT-only run (for example Saxicola rubetra 82.7, Alauda arvensis 94.9) and of the big 5 (for example Saxicola rubetra 77.1, Perdix perdix 84.1) come from the recomputation of step 1.
3. **Internal consistency.** The MSI combined index equals the geometric mean of the 11 species means in both runs (93.621222 and 96.218287); 2005 = 100 everywhere; lower <= mean <= upper; 50 and 25 replicates.

What these checks do not cover: that the model itself is right (the hindcast and the model assumptions, `improvements.md` item 21), and the assignment of the meta-model coefficients to species in section 7.5, which was made from the task order of the log files (command in section 7.5 to confirm it).
